title: perf(git-shim): remove remaining per-call readlink/bash spawns and repeated guard probes without changing verdicts (successor to #38896, unblocks #38918)
body:
## What

Cut the per-call spawn cost that the canonical Git shim (`.agents/scripts/git` → `canonical-git-command-guard.py`) still pays **without changing any policy verdict**. This is the successor to #38896, which closed on 2026-11-17 after adding a shim inode self-skip and a per-classification probe memo, but recorded no timing gain (its 20-call timing loop could not run under the worker shell policy).

## Why

#38918 (worktree archive lifecycle suite, target < 300 s, 3 slowest cases < 10 s) has exhausted its caller-side reductions: six partial PRs merged (#38919, #38930, #38931, #38935, #38944, #38961) and the in-scope Python callers now resolve admin/common dirs once per pass. Its 2026-11-18 06:16 UTC strace profile of `test_compact_preserves_git_changes_and_untracked_not_ignored` (still hitting its 60 s fixture timeout under strace) shows the remaining repeats sit in the shim and guard, which #38918 explicitly excludes:

| Repeat per case | Count |
|---|---|
| `readlink` of the git shim | 40 |
| shim `bash` wrapper launches | 22 |
| guard probe `rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir --show-toplevel` | 15 |
| guard probe `config --path --get core.worktree` | 15 |

Total: 249 git-related execs for one case. The `readlink` count suggests the #38896 inode self-skip does not cover this call path (for example a second shim generation on PATH, or the readlink happening before the inode check). Every pulse, worker and interactive `git` call pays this cost, so the gain is framework-wide.

## How

1. Re-profile on current `main`: `strace -f -qq -e trace=execve` over the case above and one plain `git rev-parse HEAD` through the shim in a linked worktree. Attribute each `readlink`/`bash` exec to its caller line.
2. Remove mechanical repeats **inside one shim/guard invocation only**: resolve native git once without `readlink` spawns (pure-bash or in-process path resolution), and reuse one combined `rev-parse` result for the guard's `--git-dir`/`--git-common-dir`/`--show-toplevel` and `core.worktree` probes when the same classification asks more than once.
3. Reference patterns: #38094 (merged `rev-parse` probes, deferred imports), #38896's merged change, and #33062 / PR #33063 (`gh` shim overhead cut with policy unchanged).
4. Measure 20 sequential calls with a script file run once (not an inline shell loop) if the worker shell policy blocks loops.

## Constraints (hard boundary)

- No verdict changes. Every case in `test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh` and `test-git-safety-guard.sh` keeps its current result.
- No cache that outlives one process (no files, env vars or daemons carrying probe results or the resolved native git between calls).
- No subcommand fast path that bypasses the guard. Classification stays in `canonical_git_policy.py` / `canonical_git_readonly.py`.
- Security-sensitive change: the PR states the threat model in one paragraph and needs the normal independent review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-git-safety-guard.sh` pass with no changed expectations.
- [ ] Before/after exec counts for the strace case above in the PR, with `readlink` and shim `bash` launches per case reduced.
- [ ] Before/after mean of 20 sequential `git rev-parse HEAD` calls through the shim in a linked worktree, same machine, in the PR.
- [ ] PR uses `Resolves` for this issue and `Ref #38918`; #38918 is then re-profiled by its own worker.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/git`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_repository.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_invocation.py`
- `.agents/scripts/runtime-env.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`

Ref #38918 (split by the pulse terminal-blocker recovery owner; caller-side reduction stays there). Ref #38896.

title: fix(backfill-status-available): never release issues carrying a blocked companion or hold label to status:available
body:
## What

`backfill-status-available.sh --apply` (the documented pulse exit cleanup in `scripts/commands/pulse.md`) sets `status:available` on any open `auto-dispatch` issue that has no `status:*` label, even when it still carries a human-owned blocked companion such as `needs-maintainer-input`. It must not release those issues.

## Evidence

During a supervisor pulse on 2026-11-18, an issue in a private managed repo had `needs-maintainer-input` but had lost its `status:blocked` label. The recovery supervisor had just recorded `wake: human_decision` for that issue, and a canonical `**Still needed (owner: maintainer)**` ask was already on the issue. The exit backfill then printed `→ status:available` for it. The pulse put the hold back with `gh-write-helper.sh issue status <N> --repo <slug> blocked`. Without that, the next deterministic pass would have dispatched a worker, which would hit the same `input_required` blocker and use up one run.

Cause: `EXCLUSION_LABELS` in `.agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh:45-51` lists only `parent-task`, `persistent`, `consolidation-task`, `routine-tracking` and `no-auto-dispatch`. It does not list the companion labels from `reference/dispatch-blockers.md` "Blocked Companion Labels" (GH#38360) or the review holds.

## Reproducer

1. Pick (or create) an open `auto-dispatch` issue in a pulse-enabled repo and give it `needs-maintainer-input` with no `status:*` label.
2. Run `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh --dry-run --repo <owner/repo>`.
3. Observed: the issue is listed as a backfill candidate; with `--apply` it gains `status:available` (seen 2026-11-18: `[backfill] <repo>#<N> → status:available` for an issue holding `needs-maintainer-input`).
4. Expected: the issue is skipped (or restored to `status:blocked`), because its companion label names a maintainer owner.

## How

- In `.agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh`, treat an issue that has no status label but has a blocked-owned or human-owned companion (`needs-maintainer-input`, `needs-dependency`, `needs-credentials`, `needs-maintainer-permissions`, `needs-ai-recovery`) as a lost `status:blocked` label. Either skip it or restore `status:blocked` through `set_issue_status`; never set `status:available`. Also exclude `hold-for-review` and `needs-maintainer-review`.
- Keep the change small: extend the exclusion list or add one companion check. Match how the search query builds its exclusions.
- Reference pattern: the companion routing in `shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh` (`blocked_needs_label_for_reason`) and the label-invariant pass in `pulse-issue-reconcile-normalize.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dry run (`backfill-status-available.sh --dry-run --repo <slug>`) does not list an `auto-dispatch` issue that has `needs-maintainer-input` and no status label.
- [ ] Status-less issues without companion or hold labels are still backfilled as before.
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh` reports nothing. Any existing test for this script still passes.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-backfill-status-available.sh`

The test path may not exist yet. If it does not, verify with a dry run against a fixture repo instead; do not add a new test harness.

title: t19105: fix(recovery): reserve queue budget for decided holds so replies, policy chan...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19105` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `priority:high`

## Outcome

fix(recovery): reserve queue budget for decided holds so replies, policy changes and retries can wake them

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`tbr_pending` (`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`, per-tier scan in `_tbr_pending_scan_tier`) scans tier 0 (entries without a standing `human_decision`) through a full rotation before tier 1 (decided entries) starts (GH#38692). Both tiers share one queue deadline. When tier 0 cannot finish inside the deadline, tier 1 is never scanned.

On this runner it has never been scanned in either mode. `pending_cursor_decided` and `rearm_cursor_decided` do not exist in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/terminal-blocker-recovery/`, although `_tbr_pending_scan_tier` saves the tier cursor before every entry check. `pending_cursor` and `rearm_cursor` were written minutes ago. The queue holds ~125 entries (~78 undecided). The pending queue window is ~29s (45s budget minus a 16s seed/unclassified reserve), and the rearm window is 45s.

Fix: reserve a share of the queue window for tier 1 whenever decided entries exist. Tier 0 stops at its own deadline (queue deadline minus the reserve, with the reserve at about a quarter of the remaining window and at least 1s), and tier 1 then runs until the queue deadline. Tier 1 gets any time tier 0 leaves unused. Classify the queue once per run, instead of calling `_tbr_entry_decided` (3 jq reads) for every file in every tier and pass.

## Why

Tier 1 is where every positive wake signal for a decided hold lives:

- A maintainer reply newer than the decision (GH#38311).
- A changed repo recovery policy (t19068).
- In rearm mode, a trusted `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` or a brief revision.

None of these can fire while tier 1 is never scanned. A maintainer who answers a decision packet gets no action, and the issue stays blocked until someone starts an interactive session. Current example: 14 `human_decision` records in one managed repo carry no policy fingerprint. That repo now declares `session_cap_split` and `brief_authority`, so t19068 should wake them for re-assessment. None has been re-assessed.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`:
  - New `_tbr_pending_classify`, run once before the tier loop: it builds the decided set from `_tbr_entry_decided` and sets a tier-0 deadline when the set is non-empty.
  - `_tbr_pending_scan_tier` takes tier membership from that set and uses the tier-0 deadline for tier 0. Hitting the tier-0 deadline marks the run incomplete and returns a distinct code, so the caller continues to tier 1. Hitting the queue deadline still stops both tiers.
  - Keep `tbr_pending` and the new functions under 100 lines each.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With decided entries queued and a window too small for tier 0, a `pending` run checks at least one tier-1 entry and writes `pending_cursor_decided`. The same holds for `rearm` and `rearm_cursor_decided`.
- [ ] With no decided entries, tier 0 keeps the whole queue window.
- [ ] The GH#39006 `--count` cursor hold behaves the same in both tiers.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- After deploy: `pending_cursor_decided` and `rearm_cursor_decided` appear in the recovery root within one pulse cycle, and decided records without a policy fingerprint in a repo that now has a policy get re-recorded with one.

</details>

title: t19106: fix(pulse): early blocker re-probe must recheck API pressure and only follow queue-side partial scans
body:
## Task


This follows up GH#39008 (PR #39009, merged as 7369e72f7a). `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh` re-probes early after a zero-count `pending --count` exit 2. Two cases are wrong:

1. **API pressure after scheduling.** `_pulse_blocker_partial_reprobe` checks `_pulse_blocker_api_pressure_active` only when it writes the deadline. If the GraphQL circuit breaker or secondary cooldown starts later, reaching the deadline still runs `pending --count` before the normal interval. The early path should check pressure again and, while pressure is active, leave the deadline file in place.
2. **Partial discovery with a fully read queue.** `pending --count` also exits 2 with count 0 when the queue pass finished and only a discovery stage (`seed`, `holds`, `unclassified`) was incomplete. GH#35945 notes the seed rarely finishes in one call, so after deploy almost every zero-count probe would re-probe every 600s, not every 3h. A persistent seed failure would repeat the same probe each time. GH#39008's premise is unread *queue* work, so only queue-side incompleteness should schedule the early probe.

Source: CodeRabbit review on PR #39011, threads on `pulse-dispatch-engine-supervisor.sh` lines 189 and 206.

title: t19107: fix(worker-lifecycle): keep Git diagnostics for two-element commands, consistent explain text, age-first root sshd check
body:
## Task


Three small defects in the GH#38997 code (PR #38999, merged as 405579ed33), from a CodeRabbit incremental review on PR #39011. Each was checked against the code on `main`:

1. **Two-element Git commands lose their diagnostics.** `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_failure.py`, `command_failure`: `len(command) < 3` returns before `_git_subcommand(command)` runs. A failure of `["git", "status"]` (or any `git <sub>` with no further args) reports only the return code. The `git status` operation and `stderr_class` (e.g. `permission-denied`) are missing.
2. **Contradictory explain text.** `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh`, `_worker_lifecycle_report_refusal`, bare-exception branch: with `WORKER_LIFECYCLE_EXPLAIN_REFUSAL=1`, the summary can print `helper=... helper_stderr_class=permission-denied`, and the next line then says "unexpected registry failure with no named condition".
3. **Predating root sshd sessions are now checked more strictly under opt-in.** `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_proc.py`, `require_predating_daemon`: a root-forked `sshd-session` skips `require_older_than_tree`. With `AIDEVOPS_PROTECTED_PROC_INSPECTION=1` it goes straight to `require_protected_references`, which can refuse (e.g. under an active maintenance plan). Before #38999, a session older than the tree passed the age check and was skipped.

Out of scope, policy already recorded on #38999: without the opt-in, a *newer* root-forked sshd session stays exempt without descriptor evidence. Accepted residual risk is limited to the opt-out default. Do not change that.

title: fix(terminal-blocker): checkpoint triage classifies transient third-party HTTP 429 rate limits as permission_required
body:
## Problem

The released-checkpoint triage in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (`_terminal_blocker_triage_unknown`, prompt near line 408) classified a transient third-party rate limit as `permission_required`.

Observed on a managed project issue (2026-11-18): the worker exited `BLOCKED` because a website's MFA step returned HTTP 429 during a publishing sign-in. The worker deliberately emitted no `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON` line and said "a rate limit fits none of the defined classes and should stay retryable". The simple-tier triage then chose `permission_required` (release comment: `reason=permission_required owner=permission-maintainer`). The release added `status:blocked` and `needs-maintainer-input`.

Effects:

- `/decisions` shows a maintainer ask, but no permission or maintainer input is needed. The only remaining step is to retry after the rate-limit window.
- The issue waits on the 12h `permission_required` window (`_TBC_PERMISSION_WINDOW_DEFAULT=43200`). If the next attempt hits another 429, the window is spent (GH#36342), and the issue then waits for a human retry instead of bounded backoff.
- `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Terminal-blocker recovery" step 5 says `permission_required` stays for runtime tool-permission denials. The triage prompt does not say so. Its pending_only clause lists "permission/access/security gate", which the model applied to a throttled sign-in.

## Proposed fix

Files to modify:

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: in the `_terminal_blocker_triage_unknown` prompt, state that `permission_required` means a runtime tool-permission or sandbox-policy denial only. Third-party HTTP 429 or other rate limits, temporary auth throttling, and transient outages are `unknown` with `pending_only` false, so they keep the bounded unclassified backoff.

title: Deterministic supersede pass and GH#33999 guard prescribe conflicting keywords when a worker closes its issue before its data PR merges
body:
## Observed

A headless worker on a managed project repo followed its issue brief's completion contract in this order: verify, post the completion comment, close the issue, then open the data PR with `Resolves #N`. The brief's contract ends "post the completion comment, and close this issue".

1. The worker opened its data PR with `Resolves #N`, then closed issue #N as completed.
2. About 4 minutes later the deterministic merge pass (GH#24399) closed the PR as superseded. Its comment said "linked issue #N is already closed by merged PR #M". PR #M was an earlier phase's PR that had not touched this PR's files. The PR's spec, brief record and work-log entry were not yet on the default branch.
3. Switching to `For #N` and running `full-loop-helper.sh merge` was refused by t2449/GH#33999 ("non-closing reference to issue #N which is not open").
4. The GH#33999 guidance comment text in `pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh` (around L712) says to switch back to `Resolves #N` when the issue closed as completed and the diff only records completion evidence. That worked: `full-loop-helper.sh merge` landed it at once.

So the supersede pass (GH#24399) and the GH#33999 guidance prescribe opposite keywords for the same state. A worker can only land the PR by racing the next deterministic pass.

## Expected

- Either the supersede pass skips a PR whose own author closed the issue as completed after the PR existed, or it cites the actual closing event instead of an older merged PR.
- Worker completion guidance should say to merge the PR with the closing keyword rather than closing the issue manually first. Or it should say the manual close must follow the PR merge.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh` (`_worker_briefed_link_kind`, GH#33999 comment text around L712)
- The deterministic superseded-PR close path (GH#24399; exact file not identified, search for "Closed by deterministic merge pass")
- Worker completion guidance in `workflows/full-loop.md` / `reference/task-lifecycle.md`

## Verification

Create a worker PR with `Resolves #N`, close #N as completed by the same session after PR creation, and run one merge pass. The PR should stay open and mergeable, or the refusal should name a single consistent keyword route.

title: t19109: fix(pulse-merge): prioritise APPROVED and clean PRs so a large backlog stops starving merge-ready work
body:
## Task


The deterministic merge pass walks each repo's open PRs in plain list order from a
persisted cursor, with no priority for PRs that are already APPROVED and
`mergeable_state=clean`. On a repo with a large PR backlog the per-pass time budget
is consumed by a handful of PRs near the cursor, so merge-ready PRs wait many cycles
and the pass reports `merged=0` while clean approved work is available.

Target repository: marcusquinn/aidevops

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

The deterministic merge pass walks each repo's open PRs in plain list order from a
persisted cursor, with no priority for PRs that are already APPROVED and
`mergeable_state=clean`. On a repo with a large PR backlog the per-pass time budget
is consumed by a handful of PRs near the cursor, so merge-ready PRs wait many cycles
and the pass reports `merged=0` while clean approved work is available.

Target repository: marcusquinn/aidevops

## Observed evidence

One Linux pulse host, aidevops v3.39.228, one private managed repo
(role `maintainer`, `pulse: true`) with 49 open PRs. Repo slug, host and author logins
are redacted as placeholders; the log lines are otherwise verbatim.

One complete pass, from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`:

```
[pulse-wrapper] Merge pass: resuming <private-repo> at PR cursor index=4 last_pr=27715 next_pr=27498
[pulse-wrapper] deterministic_merge_pass timing: repo=<private-repo> total_s=238 list_s=3
  list_state=complete mergeability_s=4 ruleset_s=5 branch_protection_s=5 stuck_detector_s=0
  merged=0 closed=0 failed=0 prs=49 enrichment_s=23 pr_s=143 trust_gate_s=32 other_s=69
  memo_skips=0 slowest_pr=#27498:143s
  slowest_stages=parse_and_validate:4,handle_conflict:0,review_and_gates:29,required_checks:5,pre_merge:26,admin_merge:73
```

Cursor state after the pass (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge-checkpoint.pr-cursor`):

```
<private-repo>|5|27498|27491
```

So 49 open PRs were listed, the cursor advanced from index 4 to 5, and nothing merged.

The single PR that consumed 143 s of the 238 s pass could not merge, by the pass's own
classification:

```
[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: unclassified non-required check '<repo-specific check>'
  is terminal-failure for PR #27498 in <private-repo> — merge blocked (GH#27137)
[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: PR #27498 in <private-repo> not ready
  (active=0, blocking_failures=1, advisory_failures=0) (GH#27137)
```

Meanwhile five PRs in the same repo were APPROVED and genuinely mergeable, and received
no verdict line in `pulse-merge.log` at all (only `gh-wrapper` read noise), i.e. they were
never evaluated. Verified directly with
`gh api repos/<private-repo>/pulls/<n> --jq '[.mergeable, .mergeable_state] | @tsv'`:

| PR | author | base | mergeable | mergeable_state |
|----|--------|------|-----------|-----------------|
| #27673 | maintainer-a | develop | true | clean |
| #27661 | collaborator-b | develop | true | clean |
| #27578 | maintainer-a | develop | true | clean |
| #27456 | collaborator-b | develop | true | clean |
| #23810 | collaborator-b | develop | true | clean |

All five carry `origin:worker` or `origin:worker-takeover`, so the GH#23238
`origin:interactive` manual-merge preference does not explain the skip. Repo role is
`maintainer`, so the contributor/read-only prefilter at
`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh:1195` does not apply either.

Note the `admin_merge:73` stage accrued on #27498 in the same pass whose `pre_merge`
stage had already classified it `not ready (blocking_failures=1)`. Worth confirming
whether that 73 s is a merge attempt that cannot succeed, or repair-dispatch time
attributed to the merge stage.

## Why this matters

`merged=0` with five approved, clean, mergeable PRs waiting is lost throughput, not a
capacity limit. The earlier fix `GH#38248: fix(pulse-merge): stop human-gated retry hints
starving merge-ready PRs` addressed a different starvation source; cursor order is a
second one.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh

## Where to look in those files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh` — PR iteration and cursor logic. Relevant
  helpers: `_pmp_pr_cursor_index_for_number` (line 184), the cursor-resume helper around
  line 217-248, `_pmp_pause_merge_pr_cursor` around line 430-460, and the enrichment
  cursor loop at line 598-614. The repo row query is at line 1316.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` — per-PR gate and merge sequencing, if the
  wasted `admin_merge` time on an already-blocked PR turns out to be a separate defect.

## Reference pattern

Follow the prioritisation precedent in `GH#38248` (commit `ed79fbb701`) and the
negative-verdict caching in `GH#38774` (commit `ff4b1df92c`, `perf(pulse-merge): cache
negative verdicts and prefilter empty repos`). A negative verdict for a PR with a known
terminal non-required failure should be cheap to re-derive on the next pass, and the
cursor should not have to pay full gate cost for it again before reaching clean approved
PRs.

Keep the existing cursor contract: it exists so a long repo backlog makes forward
progress across passes rather than restarting at index 0 each cycle. Any ordering change
must preserve that fairness property and must not reintroduce unbounded per-pass cost.

## Suggested direction (not prescriptive)

Order each repo's candidate list so PRs that are already APPROVED with
`mergeable_state=clean` are evaluated before PRs with a cached blocking verdict, while
still advancing the cursor over the remainder so nothing is permanently skipped.

## Verification

1. Shell gate: `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` and
   `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh` with zero violations.
2. Existing pass tests must stay green:
   `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-checkpoint-resume.sh`,
   `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-timing-summary.sh`,
   `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-primary-first-diagnostics.sh`.
3. Behavioural evidence: run the merge pass against a repo fixture holding one PR with a
   terminal non-required failure plus two APPROVED/clean PRs, and show from the
   `deterministic_merge_pass timing:` line that `merged` is greater than 0 and that the
   blocked PR no longer dominates `slowest_pr`.
4. Do not add new test infrastructure for this; extend the three existing pass tests
   above if coverage is needed.

title: aidevops init via a linked worktree leaves registered repos without local .aidevops.json
body:
## Problem

Repositories initialized with `aidevops init` through a linked worktree end up registered in `repos.json` but with no `.aidevops.json` in the canonical checkout. The new repository-onboarding advisory (#37845) then reports "repo has incomplete aidevops setup — run aidevops init", although init did run and its bootstrap PR merged.

## What was observed (v3.39.228, Linux)

- 4 of 7 registered private repos on one host have no `.aidevops.json` in the canonical checkout. Each has a merged bootstrap PR from a `chore/aidevops-init` branch created in a linked worktree.
- In each, `.aidevops.json` is in `.gitignore` (added by init), so the file stayed in the worktree and was lost when that worktree was cleaned up.
- The registry entries are intact (path, features, `init_scope`, runner).
- Repos initialized before `.aidevops.json` became untracked (v2.144.0 policy) still have their local file, because untracking kept the existing copy.
- `aidevops project-config restore <slug>` (#32277) previews a correct recovery for the affected repos.

## Context

- `aidevops init` calls `check_protected_branch` (`aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh`). On `main` without a TTY it auto-selects "create worktree"; with a TTY the operator can choose "continue on main". `project_root` then resolves to the worktree, and the config is written there, while registration resolves the main worktree path (`aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh`).
- `reference/repo-onboarding.md` step 1 and the agent rules (interactive sessions never edit canonical checkouts) both direct init into a linked worktree. So AI-run inits take the worktree path every time, while a maintainer running init in a terminal and choosing "continue on main" does not. This may explain why the gap has not been visible on maintainer machines; it does not appear to be platform-specific.
- Before #37845 (2026-11-12) nothing reported a missing local config, so affected repos were silent.
- The advisory's remedy, "run aidevops init", repeats the same path. It can also re-scaffold files the operator deliberately removed in the bootstrap PR (for example `DESIGN.md`, badges, `context/keywords.md`).

## Impact

- Toast noise that sends operators to a remedy that does not fix it.
- Any behaviour that reads per-repo settings from the local `.aidevops.json` falls back to defaults on these repos. The exact consequences were not measured here.

## Considerations for the design

- Where the per-repo local config should live, or come from, when init runs in a linked worktree but registers the canonical path. Consider the rule that interactive sessions never write to canonical checkouts.
- Whether the local file should remain the source of truth, given that the registry already holds most of the same settings.
- Which remedy the onboarding advisory should recommend when a repo is registered and its bootstrap PR has merged.
- Recovery for repos already affected, including ones whose `.gitignore` does not yet list `.aidevops.json` (restore currently refuses those with "Explicit safe .gitignore rule required").
- Keeping AI-run and terminal-run init paths consistent.

- How the audit should recognise repos that aidevops creates for a special purpose and that intentionally skip `aidevops init`. title: Sudo permission-approval pulse kick strips user session env; kicked pulse holds lock and every worker launch fails (manager_probe_failed)
body:
## Observed (aidevops v3.39.228, Ubuntu, systemd user-service pulse)

After `sudo aidevops approve permissions issue <N> <owner/repo> --request perm-<id> --withdraw`, `_kick_pulse_after_permission_approval` (`.agents/scripts/approval-helper-permissions.sh:401-418`) spawned a **full** pulse:

    nohup sudo -u "$SUDO_USER" -H -- "$pulse_wrapper"

`sudo -u` resets the environment, so the kicked pulse has no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`. It took the pulse lock and kept cycling, so the systemd-timer pulse could not run. Every worker launch from that instance failed:

    [dispatch_worker_launch] ERROR: selected systemd backend unavailable for #<n> (reason=manager_probe_failed rc=1 stderr=Failed_to_connect_to_user_scope_bus_via_local_transport:__DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS_and__XDG_RUNTIME_DIR_not_defined ... xdg_runtime_dir_set=no dbus_session_bus_address_set=no); detached fallback suppressed
    [dispatch_worker_launch] ERROR: worker spawn failed for #<n> rc=1; no worker submitted (GH#36390)

Five launches failed across three issues in about 10 minutes (including the issue whose permission was just withdrawn), and dispatch claims were rolled back each time. `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh status` showed the lock holder as the child of a root-owned `sudo -u <user> -H -- .../pulse-wrapper.sh` process. `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart` (SIGKILL needed for the sudo pair) and letting the systemd timer start the next pulse recovered dispatch.

The issue-approval kick (`approval-helper.sh:1104-1109`) has the same env-stripping pattern but passes `--merge-only`. It should be checked for the same class of problem if a merge pass ever needs the user bus.

## Expected

A pulse kicked from a sudo approval/withdrawal either runs with the real user's session environment or does not hold the main pulse lock. Worker dispatch from it never depends on a missing user bus.

## Suggested fix (worker decides)

- Prefer triggering the systemd-managed pulse instead of spawning a raw one: e.g. `sudo -u "$SUDO_USER" XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/<uid> systemctl --user start <pulse service>`, or just rely on the Layer-1 trigger marker plus the next timer tick. Or
- Pass `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u "$SUDO_USER")` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/<uid>/bus` explicitly through `sudo -u ... env ...`. Or
- Make the permission kick `--merge-only` like the issue-approval kick, if a full cycle is not required.
- Make the pulse refuse to take the main dispatch lock when the systemd worker backend probe fails at startup, rather than holding the lock and failing every launch.

title: cloudron-release-approval-helper: jq 1.8 @base64d rejects GitHub's wrapped base64, blocking standing release policies
body:
## What

`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process` cannot evaluate a signed standing release policy when the system `jq` is 1.8.x. Every routine Cloudron package bump stays held, even though the policy is signed and the PR is green.

## Evidence

- `jq-1.8.2` on macOS. `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --repo <owner/repo> --issue <release-request>` printed:
  `jq: error (at <stdin>:1): string ("ewogICJpZCI6ICJ4eXouYnV6...") is not valid base64 data`
  and then `approval NO_APPROVAL; no merge`. The standing policy issue verified as `VERIFIED` (`exact-snapshot`) at the same time.
- Root cause, reproduced: `jq -n '"ewogICJp\nZCI6ICJ4" | @base64d'` fails with the same error on jq 1.8.2. The same string without `\n` decodes. jq 1.8 rejects whitespace inside base64 for `@base64d`.
- The GitHub contents API returns `.content` wrapped at 60 columns with `\n`. `release_raw_contents()` (`.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`, around line 364) returns that wrapped value unchanged. System-jq callers then run `@base64d` on it: `release_manifest_versions()` (~line 375), the companion-image check (~line 466) and the catalog baseline check (~line 536).
- `cloudron_routine_bump.py:104` already strips whitespace (`"".join(entry[side].split())`) before `b64decode`, so only the jq callers are affected.
- `release_contents()` (~line 44) decodes inside `gh --jq` (gojq), which accepts newlines, so it is not affected.

## Fix

In `release_raw_contents()`, remove whitespace from `.content` before returning it, for example `--jq 'select(.type == "file" and .encoding == "base64") | .content | gsub("\\s"; "")'`. Keep the non-empty check. The exact-bytes guarantee holds because base64 whitespace carries no data.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`: `release_raw_contents()`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/` has an existing release-approval helper test, if any; extend it with a wrapped-base64 fixture only when that is the cheapest way to prove the fix.

## Verification

- `jq -n '"ewogICJp\nZCI6ICJ4" | gsub("\\s"; "") | @base64d'` decodes.
- On jq 1.8.x, `cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --repo <repo> --issue <unsigned routine request>` (dry run, without `--apply`) evaluates the policy without the base64 error.
- ShellCheck is clean.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Reopened issues keep their assignee from the finished lifecycle, and the pulse then orders them behind all fresh work. In a deep backlog they are not attempted at all.

Observed on a managed product repo (2026-11-17..18). A completion-phase worker found that two closed sibling issues had unfinished rows, so it reopened them with an explanation. `_action_rsd_single` healed both from open + `status:done` to `status:available`. In the next 10-16 hours neither issue showed up in the local pulse log, although the dispatcher made several hundred attempts on other issues in that time. The completion phase that depends on them stayed blocked.

There are two causes:

1. `_action_rsd_single` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh` sets `status:available` but leaves assignees in place. Those assignees came from the closed lifecycle and no longer hold a claim.
2. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, `_dispatch_order_claim_state_candidates` (GH#38333) counts any assignee as a claim and moves the candidate after all unclaimed work. Dispatch dedup (`_is_assigned_compute_blocking` in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-assignment.sh`, GH#18352/t1996) treats self, repo owner and repo maintainer as passive when there is no active claim, so these candidates would pass the assignee gate cheaply. GH#38333 was justified by claimed candidates that the guards rejected after 27-75s each. Passive-only assignees do not hit that cost.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh`:
  - Add `_pir_prior_lifecycle_assignees <slug> <issue> <issue_json>`. Read the issue events once with `gh api --paginate`, find the latest `reopened` time, and print each current assignee that has no `assigned` event at or after that time, comma-joined. Print nothing, and do no cleanup, if the issue was never reopened, if the events read fails, or if a timestamp is malformed. Reuse the `_PIR_ISO_UTC_RE` check from `_pir_latest_reopen_at`.
  - `_action_rsd_single`: when `restored_status` is `available` and that helper prints logins, pass `--remove-assignee <logins>` to `set_issue_status`. If that combined edit fails, heal the status alone, as before, so assignee cleanup can never block the heal. Log the removed logins on the existing "healed" line. A `blocked` restore keeps its assignees.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` `_dispatch_order_claim_state_candidates`: an assignee counts as claimed unless the candidate has all of the following, mirroring `_has_active_claim` plus `_is_assigned_compute_blocking`:
  - no `status:queued`, `status:in-progress`, `status:in-review` or `status:claimed` label
  - no `origin:interactive` without `auto-dispatch`
  - only assignees in {`$_DISPATCH_SELF_LOGIN`, the repo owner from `repo_slug`, the repo maintainer from `$REPOS_JSON`}

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh

title: browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot: hard-fails without sips/magick even when no resize is needed, and long page URLs overflow filenames (ENAMETOOLONG)
body:
## What happened

Running `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url <local dev URL> --pages "<path>?<query>" --viewports desktop --max-dim 1568 --measure-file measure.js` on Linux without ImageMagick or `sips`:

1. The capture and the `--measure-file` hook succeed and the PNG is written, but the command prints `[ERROR] No supported image tool found for guardrails (need sips or magick)` and `Screenshot guardrail enforcement failed`, then exits 1. The image (1440x900) was already within `--max-dim`, so no resize was needed.
2. With a long query string in `--pages` (about 1.5 KB of URL-encoded JSON) the page fails with `ENAMETOOLONG: name too long, open '.../before-...png'`, because the filename is built from the whole page path including the query string.

## Where

- `scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh`, `enforce_screenshot_size_guardrails` (about line 158): returns 1 as soon as neither `sips` nor `magick` exists, before it looks at any image.
- `scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh`, `get_image_dimensions` (about line 100): only `sips -g` or `magick identify`, no fallback.
- `scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh`, screenshot script template (about line 463): `const safeName = pagePath.replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/^_/, '') || 'index';` keeps `?`, `=` and `%` and has no length cap.

## Suggested change

- Read PNG dimensions from the IHDR header when neither tool exists. `od -An -tu1 -j16 -N8 file.png` yields width and height bytes (checked: gives 1440x900 for a 1440x900 capture). Require `sips`/`magick` only when an image actually exceeds `--max-dim`; otherwise return 0, optionally with a warning.
- Build `safeName` from `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` only and cap its length (for example 80 characters plus a short hash of the full path when truncated) so any URL gives a valid, stable filename.

## Verification

1. On a host without `sips`/`magick`: `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url http://127.0.0.1:PORT --pages "/" --viewports desktop --max-dim 1568` exits 0, prints no ERROR and leaves the PNG in place.
2. Same command with `--pages "/?q=$(printf 'x%.0s' {1..600})"` exits 0 and writes one PNG whose filename is under 255 bytes.
3. With `--max-dim 800` and no resize tool it still fails, with a message naming the missing tool (a resize is genuinely required).
4. `browser-qa-helper-tests.sh` stays green; add cases for 1 to 3 there.

title: pre-edit check passes but direct-write policy denies worktree edits from sessions outside the Git workspace
body:
## What

An interactive OpenCode session whose project directory is outside the trusted Git workspace (`AIDEVOPS_GIT_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, default under the home directory) gets conflicting signals. Every preparatory step succeeds, then the first real edit is denied:

1. `interactive-start-helper.sh --issue N --repo owner/repo ... --auto-dispatch` claims the issue, creates a linked worktree under the worktree base directory and prints `NEXT_STEP: cd to the worktree path and continue implementation there`.
2. `aidevops_pre_edit_check` with `workdir=<that worktree>` returns `Pre-edit check PASSED (exit 0)`.
3. The first `Edit`/`Write` into the worktree is denied: `BLOCKED by canonical write policy: cross-repository linked worktree access is limited to the trusted Git workspace. ACTION_REQUIRED=create_or_use_linked_worktree`.

The denial is correct by design (`canonical-write-policy-helper.py:95-103`, `reference/repo-organization.md` "Direct-write workspace boundary"). Two parts are wrong, though. The earlier steps report success, and `ACTION_REQUIRED=create_or_use_linked_worktree` points at the wrong remedy: the worktree already exists. The real fix is to run the session from inside the Git workspace. The session loses an issue claim, a worktree and a full investigation before it finds out it can't edit.

Observed while the session ran from a non-Git app workspace directory (an agent-chat app's workspace) and implemented an approved issue in a managed repo.

## Fix

- `pre-edit-check.sh` / the `aidevops_pre_edit_check` tool: when the session context (the plugin's project directory, not `workdir`) is outside the trusted workspace and the target is a cross-repository linked worktree, fail with the same decision as `canonical-write-policy-helper.py`. The message should say to restart the session from inside the Git workspace (the repo or its worktree).
- `interactive-start-helper.sh`: run the same probe before claiming or creating a worktree, and refuse early with that guidance.
- `canonical-write-policy-helper.py`: for this specific deny reason, emit an `ACTION_REQUIRED` value that names the actual remedy, for example `run_session_inside_git_workspace`, not `create_or_use_linked_worktree`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/canonical-write-policy-helper.py`
- `.agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`

The OpenCode plugin's pre-edit tool lives under `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`. Its exact file is unknown; find it by searching for `aidevops_pre_edit_check`.

## Verification

From a session whose project directory is outside the Git workspace:

- `aidevops_pre_edit_check workdir=<linked worktree of another repo>` returns non-zero with the restart guidance.
- `interactive-start-helper.sh` refuses before claiming.

From a session inside the Git workspace, both still pass. The existing git-safety-gate tests pass.

title: Worktree cleanup refuses every candidate: unreadable same-UID processes force cwd-visibility-degraded (removed=0 on 169 passes)
body:
## Summary

Automatic worktree cleanup has effectively stopped removing worktrees on a Linux install with ~930 linked worktrees. Across two rotated `cleanup_worktrees.log` files (169 async passes) only one pass reported `removed=1`; the other 168 reported `removed=0`. The latest pass logged `Finished-worktree reclaim: removed=0 refused=928 failed=0`, while the async summary line still printed `skip_reasons=none`.

This is not a dry run: `storage-cleanup-helper.sh all --apply` (daily timer) and `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` both run in apply mode. The removal guard refuses candidates fail-closed.

## Evidence

- Repeated log lines: `worktree-skipped: <path> — cwd-visibility-degraded — mode=recoverable-required` (`.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh:773`). The maintenance path never enters recovery (`:758-764`), and `worktree_maintenance_boundary.py:31-42` (`require_unused`) fails with `maintenance:cwd-visibility-degraded` when `collect()` reports any denied process.
- `worktree_process_proc.py:15-62` ignores unreadable processes owned by other UIDs and zombies, but treats every unreadable same-UID process as unknown (no name exemptions, by design). The cleanup user cannot `readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd` for 13 of its own processes: `systemd --user`, `(sd-pam)`, `gpg-agent`, `sshd`, `fusermount3`, `postgrest`, and privilege-dropping `php-fpm` pool workers. `python3 .agents/scripts/worktree_process_proc.py denied` lists them. While any one exists, every candidate is "degraded".
- The only bypass is the sealed managed-lifetime proof (`worktree_managed_lifetime_proof`). Sampling `python3 .agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py status <abs-path>`: of the 40 most recently modified worktrees, 8 return 0 (enrolled) and 32 return 3 (not enrolled); of the 40 oldest, 0 are enrolled. Worktrees created by interactive sessions and by routine helpers (for example the profile-readme helper, which created unenrolled worktrees within the last few hours) never enrol, so they stay permanently refused.
- The symptom is silent: the async summary reports `outcome=success removed=0 ... skip_reasons=none` while `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh:74` counted `refused=928`.

## Prior art (all closed; read before designing)

- #34843: rootless descendant-lifetime evidence; intentionally enrols only newly created Pulse worktrees and does not retroactively enrol legacy trees. Do not simply reverse that decision.
- #31882 (`PR_SET_DUMPABLE` blocked all cleanup), #32372 and #34621 (privileged CWD inspector, sudoers rule), #32832 (recovery store grows unbounded under `ptrace_scope=1`), #36543 (profile-readme helper leaking worktrees when guarded removal fails).

## Why it matters

Worktree storage grows without bound (~930 worktrees, tens of GB, backing filesystem at 96%), and the failure looks like a successful no-op.

## Proposed approach (implementer to choose; keep the fail-closed property)

1. Give every framework worktree creation path (interactive `worktree-helper-add.sh`, routine helpers such as the profile-readme helper) either managed-lifetime enrolment or an equally rootless, documented evidence rule, so new worktrees are not born permanently ineligible.
2. Define a safe, explicit disposition for the legacy backlog that does not rely on guessing unreadable processes' CWDs. Candidates: an operator-run, audited command that attests "no external same-user process uses these paths" for a reviewed list of clean, merged worktrees (reuse the recovery-archive and content-verification checks); or the kernel's busy check for bind-mounted worktrees. No process-name exemptions without an evidence rule.
3. Fix the summary: `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` should print `refused=N` and the top refusal reasons instead of `skip_reasons=none`, and a pass that refuses everything should not be labelled plain `success`. `storage-cleanup-helper.sh` should show the last pass's refused count next to "Linked worktrees: N".

## Files likely involved

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_process_proc.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_maintenance_boundary.py`
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh` (`_worktree_guard_degraded_cwd`, `worktree_managed_prepare_removal`)
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py`, `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` (summary line), `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh` (reclaim summary)
- `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh` (`_sc_dry_run_store`, `_sc_last_worktree_outcome`)
- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-temp-worktree-cleanup.sh`

## Verification

- With an unprivileged user and at least one same-UID non-dumpable process running (a setuid helper or a privilege-dropping `php-fpm` worker), a clean worktree created through the interactive helper whose branch is merged and which matches no readable process CWD or cmdline is removed or archived by `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`, and the log shows `removed>=1`.
- A worktree that is the CWD of a readable process, holds a live owner claim, has uncommitted changes, or has an open PR is still refused.
- The async summary line reports the refused count and reasons.

## Notes

- Separate and by design: `storage.worktree_archive_retention_mode` defaults to `dry-run`, so recovery-archive pruning logs `compact-retention mode=dry-run`.

**Task ID:** `t19111` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug`

## Outcome

fix(worktree-deps): skip Spotlight marker and tool-cache entries at node_modules root instead of rejecting the restore

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Worker dependency provisioning has been refusing almost every restore for a managed pnpm product repo. Since line 250000 of the local pulse log there were 406 rejections and no successful restore. 330 of them were `dependency-provision-rejected reason=unrecorded-module-file`, and about 246 dispatch launches in that repo started without `node_modules`. Those workers start without dependencies, so typecheck, lint and tests cannot run until the worker reinstalls them, if its sandbox allows that at all.

The cause is non-module entries that tools and macOS create at the root of `node_modules`:

- `node_modules/.metadata_never_index`: zero-byte Spotlight exclusion marker, regular file, dated July
- `node_modules/.vite/` and `node_modules/.vite-temp/`: Vite dependency caches (the aidevops checkout itself has `.vite-temp/`)

In `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py`, `resolution_root()` treats every direct child of `node_modules` as a package root unless it is a scope directory or a known package-manager metadata entry (`metadata_entry`). `check_package_root()` therefore rejects the marker file as `unrecorded-module-file`. It would also reject the cache directories, because they have no inventory-backed `package.json`.

This rejection is a deliberate trust boundary. Node resolves a bare specifier such as `require('.extra.js')` to `node_modules/.extra.js`, so nothing unrecorded may be copied into a resolution position, and `test_manifestless_package_roots_and_files` keeps `.extra.js` rejected. The fix must keep that boundary.

Measured scope (implementation session): the affected source `node_modules` is about 3.9 GB, against the 64 MiB copy budget. Its `du` preflight overruns the 5s timeout, so the walk runs anyway. Once these entries are skipped, the walk will reject on the byte or entry budget, or on `stale-installed-lock` while the canonical install is behind its lockfile. Workers there will still install from the lockfile, as `workflows/full-loop.md` directs. This fix removes the false rejection for sources that fit the budget. Fast provisioning for large pnpm sources is separate work.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/_worktree_dependency_snapshot.py`: add a small typed allowlist of non-module entries that are skipped at the top level of the dependency root: neither counted, copied, recorded nor inventoried, exactly like the `STALE_STAGING` skip in `Snapshot.visit`. A worker can never resolve a skipped entry, so this is strictly safer than copying it.
  - Marker files (`S_ISREG` only): `.metadata_never_index`, `.DS_Store`
  - Tool cache directories (`S_ISDIR` only, never symlinks): `.vite`, `.vite-temp`, `.cache`
  - Any other name, or an allowlisted name with the wrong file type, keeps today's handling. That means `.extra.js`, a symlinked `.cache`, and a directory named `.metadata_never_index` are still rejected.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py`: add one case covering both managers. It restores with the marker and cache directories present, asserts that the package was copied and the skipped entries were not, and asserts that a wrong-type allowlisted name (symlinked `.cache`) is still rejected. The existing `.extra.js` expectation stays unchanged.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-dependency-provision.py

- [ ] With `.metadata_never_index` (file), `.DS_Store` (file), `.vite/`, `.vite-temp/` and `.cache/` (directories) at the root of the source `node_modules`, the restore succeeds for npm and pnpm fixtures, and none of these entries appear in the worker copy.

title: Tabby 'Buzz' workspace profile is easily mistaken for a repo profile; non-repo sessions get no warning
body:
## What

The Tabby profile that GH#29530 generates, named `Buzz`, starts OpenCode in the Buzz workspace directory, which is not a Git repository. It sits in the same Projects group as repo profiles such as `cloudron-buzz-app`, and both match a `buzz` search in Tabby. An interactive repo task was started from the `Buzz` profile by mistake. Nothing warned about it until the first file edit, after the issue had already been claimed and a worktree created.

Evidence from one occurrence:

- The new tab ran `zsh -l -c 'exec aidevops opencode --tabby-shell'` with its working directory set to the Buzz workspace, and the session's `recovery.json` recorded `directory` as that workspace. `get_profile_targets()` adds exactly one profile with that working directory, `Buzz`.
- The session ran a maintainer review (read-only, which worked) and then the full loop. `interactive-start-helper.sh` claimed the issue and created a linked worktree, `pre-edit-check` passed, and then the direct-write policy denied every edit (see #39033).
- The runtime environment showed `Is directory a git repo: no`, but neither the plugin nor the launcher said anything.

## Fix

1. `tabby-profile-sync.py`: give the generated workspace profile a name that can't be mistaken for a repo, for example `Buzz agent sessions (not a repo)`. Rename an existing managed profile, identified by `profile_kind: buzz-workspace` or its exact working directory, without touching user-renamed profiles. title: Tabby profile sync: only create profiles inside the Git workspace; drop the Buzz workspace profile; heal stale Tabby venv
body:
## What

The owner has set a rule: aidevops may create Tabby profiles only for repository paths inside the trusted Git workspace (`~/Git`, overridable with `AIDEVOPS_GIT_WORKSPACE_ROOT`). Any other generated profile is a defect.

Current behaviour breaks that rule:

- GH#29530 (commit `10d43f98a3`) added `get_profile_targets()` to `.agents/scripts/tabby-profile-sync.py`. Whenever `~/.buzz` exists, it appends a `Buzz` profile (`profile_kind: buzz-workspace`) that starts OpenCode in `~/.buzz`, which is not a repository.
- That profile sits in the Projects group next to a repo profile with a similar name. A full-loop implementation session was started from it by mistake. The session claimed an issue and created a worktree, then could not edit anything (see #39033).
- The owner removed the profile by hand. It comes back on the next working `tabby-helper.sh sync`, which `setup_tabby()` in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/post-setup.sh` runs on every non-interactive `aidevops update`.

A second defect, found while verifying, currently stops that sync from running at all on an affected Mac (part 2 below). Both must ship in the same PR. If part 2 merged alone, sync would start working again and recreate the `Buzz` profile.

## Fix

### Part 1: profiles only for paths inside the Git workspace

1. `tabby-profile-sync.py`: remove the Buzz workspace target. That means the `get_profile_targets()` addition, `profile_kind: buzz-workspace`, the workspace count in `show_status()`, and the module docstring wording about detected workspaces.
2. Add one path gate for every profile target. Create a profile only when the target's real path (`expanduser` + `realpath`) is strictly inside the Git workspace root. The root itself is not a target. Resolve the root exactly as the canonical write policy does: reuse `git_workspace_root_from_environment()`, `canonical_git_workspace_root()` and `is_within_workspace()` from `.agents/scripts/canonical_write_policy_paths.py` (import or move them into a shared helper; do not re-implement). Paths in `repos.json` may be written with a leading `~` for the home directory and must still match. Skip registered repos outside the root, and have `status` print a count line for them.
3. Reconcile on sync: remove the existing generated Buzz profile only when it is provably aidevops-generated, meaning `is_aidevops_managed_profile()` returns true and the real path of its `cwd` equals `~/.buzz`. Never delete other profiles outside the root, including user-created ones such as a home-directory profile. `status` lists them as "outside Git workspace (user-owned, preserved)".
4. Remove the Buzz wording from `.agents/reference/tabby-profiles.md` (lines 10–16), from the `tabby-helper.sh` usage comment ("detected workspaces"), and from the `setup_tabby()` header comment in `post-setup.sh`. Replace it with the Git-workspace-only rule.

### Part 2: a stale isolated Tabby Python env never heals

`_bootstrap_tabby_python()` in `.agents/scripts/tabby-helper.sh` runs `python3 -m venv --copies "$TABBY_PYTHON_ENV"` over an existing env. Observed after a Homebrew patch upgrade (3.15.0 → 3.15.2):

- `venv` rewrote `bin/python3.15` but left the old `bin/python` and `bin/python3` copies, which still link to the removed `Cellar/python@3.15/3.15.0` framework. Running them fails with `dyld: Library not loaded`.
- `tabby_python()` in `.agents/scripts/tabby-python-lib.sh` then treats the env as unusable. `status` fails with "No Python with PyYAML is available", and bootstrap's `"$isolated_python" -m pip install` fails, so `sync` aborts. In non-interactive setup this shows up only as "Tabby configuration reconciliation encountered a blocker".
- Running `python3 -m venv --copies --clear <copy of the broken env>` produced a working `bin/python3` (3.15.2), confirmed on a scratch copy.

Fix: rebuild with `--clear` when the existing env's `bin/python3` cannot run, or always when bootstrapping. Keep the pinned `PyYAML==${TABBY_PYYAML_VERSION}` install and the import check.

Supersedes #39038 and PR #39042. That approach renamed the profile and kept it; the owner rejected it.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tabby-profile-sync.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_write_policy_paths.py` (only if the root helpers move to a shared module)
- `.agents/scripts/tabby-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tabby-python-lib.sh` (only if the unusable-env check lives there)
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/post-setup.sh`
- `.agents/reference/tabby-profiles.md`
- `tests/test-tabby-profile-sync.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-profile-sync.sh`

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest tests/test-tabby-profile-sync.py` passes, with cases for:
  - `~/.buzz` exists and no profile is generated
  - a repo under the root, written as an absolute path or with a leading `~`, gets a profile
  - a registered repo outside the root gets no profile and is counted in status
  - an existing managed `~/.buzz` profile is removed by sync

title: t19113: fix(permission-broker): allow designed bounded-operation status polls through...
body:
**Task ID:** `t19113` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug`

## Outcome

fix(permission-broker): allow designed bounded-operation status polls through OpenCode doom_loop instead of killing headless workers

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Headless workers die partway through finished work when they wait on a long `aidevops_bounded_operation` command. OpenCode's built-in `doom_loop` guard fires when the last three parts of the current assistant message are identical tool calls (for example `{"action":"status","operation_id":"op_…","wait_seconds":60}`). In OpenCode 1.19 each step is a new assistant message, so this fires only when one response fans out three identical calls in parallel; sequential polls across steps never trigger it. The OpenCode session DB shows workers doing exactly that before the rejection. The headless permission broker classifies `doom_loop` as non-grantable, rejects it, and the worker session ends with `permission_required`.

Evidence from one runner on 2026-11-18 (OpenCode 1.19.6):

- `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl`: six `permission_request_non_grantable` events with `permission=doom_loop tool=aidevops_bounded_operation` between 15:28Z and 18:18Z, on three managed-repo issues. Before today there were only three in two weeks.
- The worker failure excerpts for two of them show the worker had pushed commits (and in one case opened a draft PR), then polled the same running publish operation with identical `status` arguments. The log line `permission requested: doom_loop (aidevops_bounded_operation); auto-rejecting` is followed by `[WORKER_EXIT_DIAGNOSTICS] cause=permission_required`. The completion work (publish receipt, PR finalisation) was lost and the issue went back into the queue.
- The installed OpenCode binary raises `doom_loop` with `patterns:[toolName]` and `metadata:{tool, input}`, and no call ID. So the broker can see exactly which call repeated.

Designed polling is the documented way to wait on a bounded operation. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-continuation-loops.mjs` already exempts it as `isDesignedPoll()` from aidevops' own loop detector. The status/output actions are read-only and each response reports new elapsed time, so repeating them is not a loop. GH#37625 hit the same guard with `sleep 60` and was closed with a prose-only change to `pulse-sweep.md`. A deterministic rule is needed.

## How

- NEW `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-designed-poll.mjs`: export `isDesignedPollDoomLoop(request)`. It returns true only when `permission` (or the legacy `type`) is `doom_loop`, the tool (`metadata.tool`, falling back to the single entry in `patterns`) is `aidevops_bounded_operation`, and `isDesignedPoll(tool, metadata.input)` holds, which means `action` is `status` or `output`. Reuse `isDesignedPoll` from `session-continuation-loops.mjs` and do not copy the regex.
- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs`: in `handlePermissionEvent` reply `once`, and in `handlePermissionAsk` set `output.status = "allow"`, for a designed-poll doom loop. Do this before the impossible-read and capture paths, and record one non-blocking `permission_designed_poll_allowed` event, the way `recordReadOnlyRootAllow` does. Everything else is unchanged: `start`/`cancel` repeats, other tools' doom loops, and every non-`doom_loop` permission keep today's capture and reject.
- EDIT `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`: add one test. A status or output doom loop is allowed on both the event and hook paths, with no capture file. A `start` doom loop on the same tool, and a `bash` doom loop, are still captured as non-grantable and rejected.

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker-designed-poll.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/permission-broker.mjs
- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs
- TODO.md

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a headless session, a `doom_loop` ask for `aidevops_bounded_operation` with `action` `status` or `output` is answered `once` on the event path and `allow` on the hook path, and writes no permission capture.
- [ ] A `doom_loop` ask for `aidevops_bounded_operation` with `action` `start` or `cancel`, or for any other tool, is still captured as non-grantable and rejected.
- [ ] Interactive (non-headless) behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs` passes.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-permission-broker.mjs`
- After deploy: `rg '"permission":"doom_loop"' ~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl | rg -c aidevops_bounded_operation` stops growing, and `permission_designed_poll_allowed` events appear instead.

title: Reusable Linux procfs runtime-evidence harness for worktree observer changes (from GH#39034)
body:
## Description

Publishing GH#39034 (PR #39055) required `--testing-level runtime-verified` evidence for a Linux procfs change made on a macOS host. No reusable harness existed, so a one-off Python script was written and run in a local Docker image: as root it forked a root parent renamed `sshd` whose child drops to UID 1000 without exec (the kernel clears dumpability), plus a UID 1000 non-dumpable `gpg-agent`. It then ran `worktree_process_proc.py denied` and `cwdmap /proc` as UID 1000, against both the base and the branch scripts.

That base-vs-branch comparison was the evidence the critical-runtime-risk gate accepted. Future changes to `worktree_process_proc.py`, `worktree_process_attestation.py` or the lease census will need the same thing, and each session currently has to rebuild it.

## Proposed capability

A helper, for example `.agents/scripts/linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh`, that:

1. Runs a stock image such as `debian:stable-slim` or `ubuntu:24.04` with python3, using `docker run --rm` and mounting a scripts directory read-only.
2. Sets up named process fixtures: a privsep child (root parent, setuid child with no exec), an unattested non-dumpable same-UID process, and optionally a re-parented forged chain.
3. Runs the observer modes (`denied`, `paths`, `cwdmap /proc`) as an unprivileged UID and prints a stable, diffable report.
4. Takes `--base <dir>` and `--head <dir>` and prints a diff, so its output can be pasted into the `--testing` field.

## Files

- New: `.agents/scripts/linux-procfs-runtime-check.sh`, plus a fixture script next to it.

title: fix(setup): accept a native OpenCode executable at its own ~/.local/bin launcher path
body:
## What

`_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` cannot record a valid native OpenCode executable that already sits at its own launcher path (`~/.local/bin/opencode`, or `~/.local/bin/opencode2` for the isolated profile). Setup should keep a validated native executable at that path (or move it to a distinct backing path first) instead of failing the stage.

## Why

Found while triaging CodeRabbit on PR #39039 (GH#38922). When the resolved binary equals the shim path and has no managed-shim target, the function falls back to `_setup_find_valid_opencode_binary`, which skips the shim path as a candidate (`[[ "$candidate" == "$shim_path" ]] && continue`). With no other install on PATH, it returns 1, "OpenCode stable shim verification failed" is printed, and no receipt is written. The file is never modified, so nothing is damaged; the stage fails.

The limitation predates #39039: V1 uses the same binary name (`opencode`) and the same shim path, so a native V1 executable at `~/.local/bin/opencode` hits it too. #39039 adds the global-V2 path (`AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_GLOBAL_V2=1`), which inherits it.

## Reproducer

Confirmed by code path on `main` (and on PR #39039 head `991b7f900d`); not yet run as a sandbox case:

1. Sandbox `HOME`; place an executable at `$HOME/.local/bin/opencode` that prints `1.18.29` for `--version` and `opencode run [message]` for `--help` (pattern: the `SHIM` heredocs in `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`). Ensure no other `opencode` is on PATH.
2. Source the setup modules as `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` does and run `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1 setup_opencode_cli`.
3. Expected: the executable is recorded. Actual (by code): `_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` → `resolved_bin == shim_path`, no managed target → `_setup_find_valid_opencode_binary` skips the shim path → return 1 → "OpenCode stable shim verification failed".

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`

1. In `_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim` (`rg -n "^_setup_ensure_opencode_stable_shim" .agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`), handle the branch where `resolved_bin` is the shim path, has no managed target (`_setup_opencode_managed_shim_target` is empty), and passes `_setup_validate_opencode_binary`. Preferred: move the native executable to a framework-owned backing path (e.g. under `~/.aidevops/`) atomically, then write the managed launcher pointing at it. Alternative: record the native executable as-is and skip the launcher write. Pick one and record the trade-off in the PR (moving keeps the launcher contract; keeping avoids touching a user-owned file).
2. Keep current behaviour for managed launchers and for executables outside `~/.local/bin`.
3. Never delete or overwrite a native executable before the replacement launcher validates (the existing temp-shim/`mv -f` pattern).

## Acceptance

- In the sandbox of `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh`, a fake native executable at `$HOME/.local/bin/opencode` that prints `opencode v2.3.0`, with no other `opencode` on PATH: `setup_opencode_runtimes` exits 0, `.opencode-bin-resolved` names a path that runs that executable, and `--version` still prints `opencode v2.3.0`.
- The same case for a V1 native executable (`1.18.29`) under `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_PROFILE=v1`.
- Existing cases in `test-opencode-v2-setup.sh` and `test-opencode-runtime-profile.sh` still pass; ShellCheck clean.

## Context

- Source: review comment on PR #39039 by @coderabbitai (`tool-install.sh` around `_setup_opencode_global_v2_cli`).
- `setup.sh` runs under `set -Eeuo pipefail` and calls `_time_step "$SETUP_STAGE_OPENCODE" setup_opencode_runtimes` unguarded, so a failure here aborts the rest of non-interactive setup. That makes this worth fixing, although it is rare (most installs live in npm/bun/Homebrew/`~/.opencode/bin`).

title: pre-merge-gate omits the approval command when the NMR hold reports as the maintainer-gate status
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate 38953 marcusquinn/aidevops`, for an external fork PR whose only failing required check is the live `needs-maintainer-review` hold, prints:

    [ERROR] PR #38953 has terminal required-check failures at the current head

It prints no approval command. `gh pr checks 38953 --required` shows that the failing check is named `maintainer-gate` (commit-status context); every other required check passes.

`workflows/review.md` "External PR authority preflight" requires the preflight to print the mixed `sudo aidevops approve batch issue:N pr:N... OWNER/REPO` command, and forbids composing it by hand. So an external PR with a repaired head cannot get its approval command.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate 38953 marcusquinn/aidevops`

**Actual output:**

    [ERROR] PR #38953 has terminal required-check failures at the current head

Steps:

1. Pick an external fork PR that has passing CI and a live `needs-maintainer-review` label (here #38953 at head `24c226d036`).
2. Run `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate <PR> <owner/repo>`.
3. It prints only the terminal-failure error line and no approval command.

Predicate check: `printf '%s' '[{"name":"maintainer-gate"}]' | jq 'all(.[]; .name == "gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate")'` returns `false`.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh` `cmd_pre_merge_gate` (around line 602-607) runs `_full_loop_report_external_authority_preflight` only when every terminal failure is named exactly `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`. The gate publishes two names: the workflow CheckRun `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` and the stable commit-status context `maintainer-gate` (`.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml:132-144`). Branch protection requires `maintainer-gate`, so that name is what the required-check query returns.

`pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:25-27` already treats the family as `maintainer-gate`, `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` and `gate / Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate`.

## Fix

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`: accept any member of that three-name family in the authority-only diagnostic. A mix of family members still qualifies; any non-family failure still prints no command. This is diagnostic only and never turns a failure into readiness.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh` `test_pre_merge_authority_check_failure`: assert that the command is printed for `maintainer-gate` and for the legacy display name, and that it is still withheld for a family member mixed with `lint`.

## Verification

    bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh
    shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh

Live: `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate 38953 marcusquinn/aidevops` prints the batch approval command.

body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` for GH#38959 failed its Node validator twice. The failing run was `npm run test` in `.agents/scripts`, and the failing file both times was `tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs` (2.4-2.7 s; 100 passed, 1 failed). The branch does not touch team-interface code.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 38959 ...` (Node validator stage) on a host with load average about 100 on 16 cores.

**Actual output:**

    [ERROR] [validators] CHECK FAILED (exit 1): npm run test (.agents/scripts)
    ℹ tests 103 / pass 100 / fail 1 / skipped 2
    ✖ tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs (2695.387625ms)
      'test failed'

The failure is intermittent and load-dependent. It did not reproduce in six controlled runs on the same branch:

- the file alone;
- `node --test tests/*.mjs`;
- `npm run test`;
- the plugin and scripts suites concurrently, then sequentially;
- under GNU `timeout`;
- the validator's own `_run_scoped_node_checks`, sourced from `full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`.

The host load average was about 100 on 16 cores when the failures occurred. A third `commit-and-pr` on the unchanged commit passed, and created PR #39066.

The validator keeps only `tail -20` of `command-N.log` (`full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh:285-286`) and deletes the snapshot directory afterwards, so the failing assertion text was lost.

## Likely cause

Two wall-clock budgets in the test:

- `invokeAdapterRead(..., {timeoutMs: 1000})` at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs:366`, around child `plutil` and `sqlite3` reads;
- `{timeoutMs: 20}` at `:639`, which must abort before the child read completes.

Under heavy load, the 1000 ms budget can expire before the reads finish. Unverified: confirm with the captured assertion first.

## Fix

1. `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`: on `CHECK FAILED`, print the `not ok` blocks with their diagnostics (or keep the log path) instead of only `tail -20`, so the next failure is diagnosable.
2. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs:366`: if the captured assertion is `adapter_timeout`, raise the success-path budget (for example 10000 ms). The success path only needs a generous upper bound. Keep the 20 ms abort test as it is.

## Verification

    node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-adapter.mjs

Then run the same test under load, for example alongside the plugin suite at low concurrency: no failures over five runs. A deliberately failing assertion must show its message in the validator output.

body:
**Task ID:** `t19114` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `bug` `priority:high` `interactive`

## Outcome

fix(checkpoints): resume a continuation review worktree that is only ahead of the PR head with unpushed commits

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

A stale-draft continuation worker that commits locally but exits before its single final push leaves the review worktree one or more commits **ahead** of the verified PR head. The next continuation dispatch treats that worktree as diverged and refuses to launch (`existing_review_worktree_diverged`, `retry_class=retryable_infrastructure`). The refusal repeats after every short cooldown, so the draft never moves and the linked issue stays blocked by its draft checkpoint. Every pulse round still spends a full dispatch ceremony on that issue before the draft-checkpoint block fires.

The continuation prompt already expects this case. `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` tells the worker to save a recovery bundle after each commit and "on resume keep and verify unpushed local commits, never reset them away". But `_prrts_reconcile_existing_worktree_head` in `pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh` only accepts a worktree that is behind the PR head (fast-forward). A worktree that contains the PR head plus unpushed commits fails the `merge-base --is-ancestor "$actual_head" "$head_oid"` check and is rejected as diverged.

Evidence from one runner on 2026-11-18:

- A draft PR in a private managed repository: the continuation worker launched at 18:58Z, committed one commit on top of the verified PR head at 19:25Z, and exited at 19:39Z with no push and no terminal-state command. Since 20:07Z every attempt logs `skipped — existing review worktree cannot fast-forward to verified PR head`. `git log` in the worktree shows exactly one commit ahead of the PR head, which is not diverged. An earlier draft in the same repository was in the same one-commit-ahead state and needed an interactive session to finish and merge it.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.log`: 833 `outcome=existing_review_worktree_diverged` outcomes in total, and 11 refusals across 6 PRs from 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-18.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`: the linked issue was re-attempted by the issue dispatcher at 371s, 40s and 70s of ceremony per attempt, each ending with `blocked:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`. Across the log, `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` and `stale_draft_checkpoint` attempts used about 22 hours of dispatch ceremony time over 5.7 days.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh`, `_prrts_reconcile_existing_worktree_head`: after the existing claim, dirty-state preservation, exact-head fetch and clean/branch re-check, add one case before the diverged refusal. When the dispatch is a checkpoint continuation (`_prrts_repair_linked_issue "$pr_number"` is non-empty) and `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$head_oid" "$actual_head"` holds, keep the worktree as it is, log how many unpushed commits are resumed, and return 0. The worker then starts with `AIDEVOPS_PR_REPAIR_HEAD_SHA` set to the verified remote head. Its exact-target fence and single fast-forward push still apply, and the prompt already says to keep the unpushed commits.
- Leave all other cases unchanged. A truly diverged worktree is still refused. Ordinary review-thread workers, whose prompt has no resume contract, are still refused. So are live or unverified owners and dirty state that cannot be preserved.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh
- TODO.md

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For a checkpoint continuation whose clean, exclusively claimed worktree is ahead of the verified PR head, dispatch launches the worker in that worktree without resetting it, and the log names the resumed commit count.
- [ ] A worktree whose HEAD neither contains nor is contained by the verified head is still refused with `existing_review_worktree_diverged`.
- [ ] An ordinary review-thread dispatch (no linked issue) with an ahead worktree is still refused.
- [ ] The existing worktree tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh` pass, and ShellCheck reports nothing on the edited file.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner-worktree.sh`
- After deploy: the next continuation for the affected draft logs the resume line rather than `cannot fast-forward`, and new `existing_review_worktree_diverged` outcomes in `~/.aidevops/logs/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.log` are only true divergences.

</details>
