title: DataForSEO SERP calls: support resolve_poisoned_results and resolve_goto_urls (poisoned Google results, wrapped links)
body:
## Description

DataForSEO announced on 2026-11-16 that Google returns "poisoned" result pages to automated requests: legitimate organic listings are replaced with other results, which causes false ranking drops and wrong SERP analysis. They added `resolve_poisoned_results` to every Google Organic SERP task (Standard and Live, regular/advanced/HTML). It cross-checks organic results against Google's Web mode and replaces affected rows; replaced rows carry `from_web` in their `checks` array. It costs one extra SERP page on every task, whether or not poisoning is found ($0.002 → $0.004 for a live, normal-priority, depth-10 task).

Separately, since about 2026-11-03 Google often returns organic links as opaque `https://google.com/goto?url=<token>` wrappers with `domain: google.com`. DataForSEO's `resolve_goto_urls` returns the real address at no extra charge (adds up to 40 s; max turnaround 260 s).

The framework's DataForSEO SERP paths use neither option and the docs do not mention either problem:

- `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh` — `dataforseo_serp_organic` (lines 178-199 in 3.39.229) posts `serp/google/organic/live/regular` with `depth: 10` and no resolve flags. `serp_organic_normalized` (lines 353-357) then reads `.url` for each organic row, so `keyword-research-helper.sh serp-compare` can show `google.com/goto` wrappers for DataForSEO (they never match Serper/SerpAPI URLs) and can compare a poisoned DataForSEO page against the other providers.
- `.agents/seo/dataforseo.md` — the "SERP Results" example (lines 82-89) posts `live/advanced` without either flag and there is no note on poisoned pages, wrapped links, or the extra charge.

Observed downstream (a private project with two DataForSEO SERP tools, audited 2026-11-18): 77% of organic rows in 171 saved `live/advanced` captures were `google.com/goto` wrappers, and a rank tracker showed an exact-match brand query flipping between #1 and not ranked week to week while Google Search Console held average position 1.0-1.7. Adding both flags there was cost-neutral by dropping unused depth (20 → 10).

## Expected Behavior

1. `dataforseo_serp_organic` sends `"resolve_goto_urls": true`, so `serp-compare` gets real URLs from DataForSEO.
2. `dataforseo_serp_organic` sends `"resolve_poisoned_results": true` by default (it doubles the cost of the 10-result call), with a documented way to turn it off. Maintainer decision: default on, or opt-in flag.
3. Optionally, `serp_organic_normalized` adds `restored: true` for rows whose `checks` include `from_web`.
4. `seo/dataforseo.md` adds both flags to the SERP example and a short "Poisoned SERPs and wrapped links" section: what each flag does, the per-task charge, that `resolve_poisoned_results` cannot be combined with `udm=web`/`udm=14`, that only organic rows are replaced (PAA/AI Overview come from the original page), and a reminder that billing is per 10 results so callers should not request depth they do not read.

## Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh` — `dataforseo_serp_organic` heredoc (add the two keys); optional `from_web` mapping in `serp_organic_normalized`
- `EDIT: .agents/seo/dataforseo.md` — SERP example and new section
- Possibly `EDIT: .agents/seo/keyword-research.md:162` if the provider table should note the SERP options

`rg -n "serp/google/organic" .agents` found only these three references in 3.39.229.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh`
- One paid call (~$0.004): `keyword-research-helper.sh serp-compare "<keyword>" --provider dataforseo --json` returns no `google.com/goto` URL, and the raw response `tasks[0].data` echoes both flags.

## Sources

- DataForSEO update, 2026-11-16: https://dataforseo.com/update/detect-and-resolve-poisoned-google-results-with-dataforseo-serp-api
- Endpoint parameters (`resolve_goto_urls`, `resolve_poisoned_results`, `checks` values): https://docs.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/live/advanced/

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.39.229
- **Latest version**: 3.39.229
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.3.9(1)-release

title: gh-checks-wait-helper keeps polling a PR already merged by native auto-merge, so the chained merge/release reconcile never runs
body:
## Description

`gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait <PR> --repo <slug> --all` keeps polling after the PR has been merged by GitHub native auto-merge. It stops only when its 1800s timeout expires.

Observed 2026-11-18 on protected release PR #39067 (v3.39.230):

- The release helper opened #39067 with native auto-merge enabled, using a merge commit.
- `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait 39067 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --all; full-loop-helper.sh merge 39067 ...` was started as the documented follow-up.
- GitHub auto-merged #39067 at 21:03:39Z. The waiter was still polling about 10 minutes later because the `--all` aggregate contexts (`Complexity Analysis`, `Framework Validation`) were still reported as non-terminal.
- The chained `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, which auto-reconciles the release lane after a merge, never ran. The lane stayed in `remote-publication` until `aidevops release reconcile 39055` was run by hand. Meanwhile another session saw `RELEASE_EXECUTOR dead` and nearly reconciled the same lane.

## Reproducer

1. Pick any PR that native auto-merge merged while at least one optional/aggregate check context was still non-terminal. #39067 is a real case: it merged at 21:03:39Z while `Complexity Analysis` and `Framework Validation` were still pending.
2. Run `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait 39067 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --all` while a context is still pending.
3. Observed: the helper keeps polling (on 2026-11-18, `ps` showed it at 29:41 elapsed, about 10 min after the merge) and does not exit until the 1800s timeout. With the documented chain `wait ...; full-loop-helper.sh merge N`, the merge/reconcile step is delayed until that timeout.

## Expected Behavior

When the PR is no longer open, the waiter stops polling:

- `MERGED`: print a terminal line such as `MERGED: PR #N merged at <time>; check wait not required` and exit 0. The chained `full-loop-helper.sh merge` then sees the merge and runs its post-merge release reconcile (that path already handles "PR already merged by native auto-merge").
- `CLOSED` (not merged): exit non-zero with a clear message.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`, in `wait_for_checks()` (the loop starts around line 832). Each pending poll, or at least each `max_interval` poll, should do one cheap state read (`gh pr view N --repo R --json state,mergedAt`, or reuse whatever `verified_head_sha` already fetches) and return before the timeout check.
- The test pattern to follow is the existing helper suite (`rg -l gh-checks-wait-helper .agents/scripts/tests/`). Add one case: a merged PR with a still-pending optional context returns 0 promptly.

## Verification

body:
**Task ID:** `t19115` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `priority:high`

## Outcome

fix(checkpoints): a trusted terminal-blocker re-arm never releases a blocked worker draft, even for a maintainer retry

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

A worker that releases an issue as `blocked` after opening a draft leaves the draft as a checkpoint. The draft then holds the issue until someone publishes a revision-bound `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` line. Terminal-blocker recovery can later re-arm that issue, either for a maintainer retry directive (`trusted_retry`) or for a brief revision after the blocker (`revision_changed`). It posts its receipt and projects `status:available`. The checkpoint path ignores that re-arm. `_pcc_blocked_attention` posts or re-finds `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` and the draft stays held, even when the approval template validates (`refusal=none`).

The two opt-in policy routes in `_pcc_policy_route` do not cover this case either. `_pcc_resolve_decision` needs a `reason=decision` finding. `_pcc_unknown_pending_work` needs a `CHECKPOINT_UNKNOWN_TRIAGE pending_work` marker bound to the current brief, and a revised brief by definition no longer matches it. Without the policy, the unknown digest also needs that marker. So a re-armed blocked checkpoint has no route at all. A maintainer retry directive, the strongest human signal available, is silently ignored, and the issue looks healthy (`status:available`) while nothing can run.

Evidence from one runner on 2026-11-18:

- Census of open drafts held by blocked-checkpoint attention across pulse repos: 9 open. Of those, 4 already have a trusted re-arm receipt after the blocked release: 2 `trusted_retry`, 1 `revision_changed` and 1 `unevidenced_permission_window`. All 4 show `refusal=none` in the attention marker, and none has an approval. The other 5 have no re-arm.
- One worked example in a private managed repository: blocked release 14:30Z (`reason=unknown`). At 16:03Z the recovery supervisor repaired the brief and wrote "continue draft PR, do not restart; cause: environment, not brief". At 17:03Z a runner posted `terminal-blocker-rearmed` (`reason=revision_changed`). At 17:04Z it posted `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION ... refusal=none`. More than 50 hours later the draft is untouched and every pulse round spends a dispatch ceremony ending in `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`: 35 distinct drafts reached `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS`, with zero `UNKNOWN_CHECKPOINT_APPROVED` outcomes.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-decision-resolver.sh`: in `_pcc_policy_route`, call a new `_pcc_rearmed_checkpoint_route` after `_pcc_resolve_decision` and before `_pcc_unknown_pending_work`. A trusted re-arm is newer evidence than the release-time triage. The new route returns 0 only when an approval is published or already valid.
- NEW function `_pcc_rearmed_checkpoint_route` in the same file, modelled on `_pcc_unknown_pending_work`:
  1. Find the newest unedited comment, created after the blocked release `$release`, that contains both `<!-- aidevops:terminal-blocker-rearmed key=` and a `terminal-blocker-rearm-reason` line with `reason=trusted_retry` or `reason=revision_changed`. Exclude `unevidenced_permission_window` and `lifecycle_recovered`. Neither shows that the blocker was addressed.
  2. #aidevops:trust-boundary: the receipt poster, the publishing login and the checkpoint runner need current `admin|maintain|write` permission. For `trusted_retry`, also require an unedited OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directive between the release and the receipt, posted by a login with write permission. For `revision_changed`, require the issue author to have write permission: only the author or a write collaborator can edit an issue body, so every revision is then trusted.
  3. Run the same gates as `_pcc_unknown_pending_work`: `_pr_checkpoint_pr_metadata_is_eligible`, then open/unassigned/`auto-dispatch`/no protective hold on the issue. Generate the template with `_pcc_approval_template` and check that its `head` and `brief_sha256` match the current head and brief.
  4. Reserve `refs/aidevops/checkpoint-rearm/<issue>/<receipt>` atomically: two runners publishing would leave an ambiguous approval. Then publish through `_pcc_publish_policy_approval` and print `REARMED_CHECKPOINT_APPROVED pr=… head=… release=… reason=… receipt=…`.
  5. On by default, matching the re-arm's own trust decision. A repo opts out with `checkpoint_policy.auto_continue_rearmed: false`. Do not touch `_pcc_unknown_digest`.
- EDIT `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: add a short "Re-armed blocked checkpoints" subsection covering the evidence, authority, gates and bounds.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh`, following the `test_unknown_pending_policy` pattern. Cover `trusted_retry` and trusted `revision_changed` publishing exactly once, and a lost reservation not republishing. None of these may publish: a receipt from a non-write poster, a non-write retry or issue author, a COLLABORATOR or edited retry, an older or edited receipt, permission-window and lifecycle reasons, an assigned or held issue, a moved head, or an opted-out repo.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-unknown-digest.sh
- .agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-dispatch.sh
- TODO.md

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A blocked worker draft whose issue has a newer, write-authorised `trusted_retry` re-arm receipt and a validating template gets exactly one `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` line through `gh-write-helper.sh`, with or without checkpoint policy. The next dispatch round continues the exact head through `dispatch-approved`.
- [ ] A `revision_changed` re-arm publishes the same way when the issue author has write permission; with an outside author it never publishes.
- [ ] No approval is published for: a receipt, retry or brief from a login without write permission; a receipt older than the blocked release; `unevidenced_permission_window` or `lifecycle_recovered` reasons; an assigned or held issue; a template whose head or brief no longer matches; or a repo with `auto_continue_rearmed: false`.

title: keyword-research: detect_weaknesses reads wrong JSON path, always reports 0 for DataForSEO SERP data
body:
## What

`detect_weaknesses` in `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-analysis.sh:40-70` always reports 0 weaknesses for DataForSEO SERP data. Extended keyword research (the weakness and score columns) is therefore silently wrong.

## Why

The caller at `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-analysis.sh:582-586` passes the raw `dataforseo_serp_organic` response, shaped `{"tasks":[{"result":[{"items":[...]}]}]}`. `detect_weaknesses` reads top-level `.items[]?`, which matches nothing, so every count falls back to 0. Two more problems on the same path:

- `domain_score`/`page_score` (`:594-596`) read `items[0]`, which may be a non-organic item (featured snippet, PAA) rather than the top organic result.
- `main_domain_rank` and `backlinks_count` may not exist on `serp/google/organic/live/regular` items at all. Confirm the field names in the current DataForSEO docs (on `advanced`, rank data may sit under `rank_info`).

Found while reviewing #39070, which changes the same request builder. This defect exists independently of that change.

## How

1. In `detect_weaknesses`, select organic rows from the envelope: `.tasks[0].result[0].items[]? | select(.type == "organic")`. This is the same selection `serp_organic_normalized` uses in `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh:355`.
2. In the score lookups at `:594-596`, use the first organic row instead of `items[0]`.
3. Check every field read (`main_domain_rank`, `backlinks_count`, `page_rank`) against the current DataForSEO SERP response. Map each to the correct field, or remove the checks whose data `live/regular` does not return. Do not invent fields.

## Files

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-analysis.sh` — `detect_weaknesses` (`:40-90`) and the extended-research score lookups (`:582-606`)

## Reproducer

Offline, no API call. A minimal DataForSEO envelope with one non-HTTPS organic row:

```bash
printf '%s' '{"tasks":[{"result":[{"items":[{"type":"organic","url":"http://example.com/","rank_group":1}]}]}]}' \
  | jq -c '{current_path: ([.items[]? | select(.url | startswith("http://"))] | length),
            envelope_path: ([.tasks[0].result[0].items[]? | select(.type=="organic") | select(.url | startswith("http://"))] | length)}'
# => {"current_path":0,"envelope_path":1}
```

`current_path` is the selector `detect_weaknesses` uses at `:67`. It misses the row.

title: pulse-merge defers forever to a stale native auto-merge request on a CLEAN, all-green PR
body:
## Observed

When a PR's GitHub native auto-merge request was enabled while the PR was `BLOCKED`, GitHub may never fire it after the blocker clears. Clearing a blocker by changing a branch ruleset does not raise a check or push event. The deterministic merge pass then defers to GitHub on every cycle, indefinitely.

Evidence from one managed repo (private, so no name here):
- Auto-merge was enabled on 2026-11-15T16:40Z while a ruleset required a stale check name, so the PR was `BLOCKED`.
- An admin fixed the ruleset. For about 3 days after that, the PR read `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` with every required check `SUCCESS`, and it stayed unmerged.
- Each cycle `pulse.log` logged `worker-briefed auto-merge ... passed all gates`, then `auto_merge already set, deferring to GitHub (t3070)`.
- `full-loop-helper.sh merge N SLUG --squash` merged it on the first try.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` around line 1817-1843: when auto-merge is already set and all required checks pass (`pending_count == 0`), the function always logs the t3070 deferral and returns 0. Nothing checks for a request that is older than a threshold while the PR is `CLEAN`.

## Fix

In that branch, when `pending_count == 0`, `mergeStateStatus == CLEAN`, and `autoMergeRequest.enabledAt` is older than a threshold, do not defer. Two options:
- fall through to the normal guarded merge path, the same call `full-loop-helper.sh merge` makes;
- or disable and re-enable auto-merge once per head SHA, to re-trigger GitHub.

The threshold could reuse `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_AUTO_MERGE_STUCK_SECONDS` or a sibling knob (for example 30 min). All existing gates still apply.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` (the auto-merge-set branch near the t3070 log line)
- tests beside the existing t3070/t3567 merge-process tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/`

## Verification

A fixture PR has `autoMergeRequest.enabledAt` older than the threshold, all required checks `SUCCESS` and `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`. The pass must attempt the merge instead of logging `deferring to GitHub (t3070)`. With checks pending it must keep the existing t3567 behaviour.

title: t19116: perf(pulse): reserve a dispatch slot at the claim, not at ceremony start, so rejection checks run in parallel
body:
## Task


perf(pulse): reserve a dispatch slot at the claim, not at ceremony start, so rejection checks run in parallel

`_dispatch_max_loop` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`) reserves a worker slot for every in-flight ceremony: `while ((successes_so_far + ${#_pids[@]} >= effective_slots))`. `_dispatch_max_compute_base_parallel` and `_dispatch_run_priority_phase` also clamp ceremony concurrency to the slot budget, and a 1-slot phase falls back to the serial `_dispatch_floor_loop`. A ceremony holds that reservation for its whole run, but most candidates are rejected by read-only dedup layers well before the first persistent write (the layer-7 claim in `_dlw_claim_lock_after_canary`). When few slots are free, which is the steady state on a busy runner, rejections are evaluated one at a time. Free slots stay idle while 80-110 candidates wait.

Evidence from one runner, 2026-11-17 00:00Z to 2026-11-18 22:30Z (`~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`, `pulse.log`, `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`):

- Worker occupancy averaged about 6-7 concurrent workers against `simultaneous_target_final=20`. 22% of the last 600 `Dispatch_capacity` samples had `active_workers=0`, and the median was about 6.
- Each round had plenty of candidates: `Dispatch_max: available=10..20, candidates=86..116`. Over the last 30 rounds, 743 candidates were processed and 203 dispatched (27% yield).
- `dedup.ceremony_total` averaged 233.6s (n=967). Rejected candidates spent 10-180s in `dedup.dedup_check` first.
- One 80-minute cycle (`20261118T183602Z-76726`) ran from about +3200s to +4900s in strict sequence. Each next candidate started when the previous one ended (for example, busy 34s then gap 38s, busy 33s then 28s, busy 38s then 32s). 37 candidates went through serially and 9 launched.
- REST-core serial mode is not the cause: 1 of the last 45 rounds ran `mode=serial`, and REST headroom was 3,567/5,000.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`_dispatch_max_loop` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`) reserves a worker slot for every in-flight ceremony: `while ((successes_so_far + ${#_pids[@]} >= effective_slots))`. `_dispatch_max_compute_base_parallel` and `_dispatch_run_priority_phase` also clamp ceremony concurrency to the slot budget, and a 1-slot phase falls back to the serial `_dispatch_floor_loop`. Evidence from one runner, 2026-11-17 00:00Z to 2026-11-18 22:30Z (`~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-stages.tsv`, `pulse.log`, `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`):

- Worker occupancy averaged about 6-7 concurrent workers against `simultaneous_target_final=20`. 22% of the last 600 `Dispatch_capacity` samples had `active_workers=0`, and the median was about 6.

- `dedup.ceremony_total` averaged 233.6s (n=967). Rejected candidates spent 10-180s in `dedup.dedup_check` first.

- REST-core serial mode is not the cause: 1 of the last 45 rounds ran `mode=serial`, and REST headroom was 3,567/5,000.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`:
  1. Add a launch-slot semaphore. `_dispatch_max_loop` creates a private directory holding `budget=effective_slots`. `_dispatch_launch_slot_acquire <issue> <repo>` takes `slot.N` atomically with `mkdir` and records `held.<key>`. `_dispatch_launch_slot_settle <issue> <repo> <rc>` keeps the slot on success, keeps it on 124 (worker state unknown after the per-candidate timeout kill) and releases it otherwise. `_dispatch_launch_slots_free` returns budget minus taken slots. title: source_access_blocked releases are labelled needs-credentials and routed to 'aidevops secret set', contradicting the worker contract
body:
## Problem

`source_access_blocked` releases are labelled `needs-credentials`, and the release text routes the maintainer to "provision on a runner with `aidevops secret set NAME`". The worker contract says this class must never mean missing credentials. Maintainers therefore get the wrong fix, and the `/decisions` credentials queue fills with items no secret can resolve.

Workers also use the class for questions that one named person can answer, such as "has this programme retired?". Those should be `input_required` with a `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_QUESTION`.

## Evidence (one managed project repo, 2026-11-18)

- `scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:654`: `source_access_blocked | credentials | missing_secret)` maps to `$BLOCKED_NEEDS_CREDENTIALS`.
- `scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh:173-182`: `source_access_blocked` covers external refusals (HTTP 403, bot challenge, DNS, TLS or origin failure, removed page), and "Never use it for missing local credentials or runner-local account failures".
- 10 open issues in that repo carry `needs-credentials` from a `source_access_blocked` release (same blocker fingerprint across different runners and hosts). None needs a secret:
  - Cloudflare 525 origin TLS failure: 2 issues. This is a host outage and fits a time-based revisit.
  - HTTP 403 anti-bot or paywall: 3 issues. These need a permitted capture or an alternative source.
  - Programme identity question: 1 issue. The official URL redirects to the organiser's working awards index, and the worker's dossier reopen condition was "a maintainer confirms the programme's current official site, or confirms it has been retired". One maintainer comment answered it.
  - Official root loads (HTTP 200) and the denial was on another page: 3 issues.
  - No official URL in the brief: 1 issue.

## Proposed fix

1. `scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh`: route `source_access_blocked` to its own hold label (for example `needs-source-access`, with colour and description in `scripts/label-sync-helper.sh`), or to an existing non-credentials hold. Give it release text such as "Needed: a permitted capture, an alternative official source, or the host recovering. Owner: access owner." Keep `credentials | missing_secret` on `needs-credentials`.
2. Update every consumer of the hold-label set: `scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` (lines ~108 and ~1302), `scripts/maintainer-decisions-helper.sh` (`MD_HOLD_LABELS`), `scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh:108`, `scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:1586`, `scripts/issue-sync-helper-labels.sh:223`, `scripts/backfill-status-available.sh:55`, `scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh:147-155`. Existing labelled issues need a one-time migration, or must keep working under the old label.
3. `scripts/headless-runtime-contract.sh` (around line 176): when the reopen condition is a question one named person can answer, such as programme identity, retirement or the canonical site after a redirect to a working page, emit `input_required` with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_INPUT_OWNER` and `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_QUESTION`, not `source_access_blocked`. A redirect to a working page is not an access refusal.
4. Consider letting `terminal-blocker-trigger-revisit.sh` revisit host-outage source blocks (5xx/525/DNS) on its normal backoff. Line 160 of `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` currently says source-access holds are never revisited, so a host that comes back stays blocked until someone notices.

## Verification

- `scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-claim-release-retry.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` pass, with cases added for the new mapping.

title: Model availability probe reports no-key on OpenCode 2 (no auth.json), blocking all Pulse dispatch
body:
## Summary

On OpenCode 2.x, `model-availability-helper.sh` reports every provider as `no-key`, so Pulse can never dispatch a worker: `resolve standard` / `resolve thinking` fail with "No available model for tier ... (configured candidates and extended chain exhausted)".

## Evidence

- aidevops v3.39.225 (also checked `model-availability-helper.sh` at tag v3.39.232: same code path), OpenCode v2.3.0, macOS.
- `opencode auth list` shows `Anthropic  OAuth  stored`.
- `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` does not exist on this install; OpenCode 2 keeps credentials in its own store (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`).
- `~/.aidevops/oauth-pool.json` has 1 healthy Anthropic account (`model-accounts-pool status`: available 1, auth errors 0, token endpoint OK).
- `model-availability-helper.sh probe anthropic --force` → `anthropic: no API key configured`; `status` → anthropic/openai/opencode-go all `no-key`.
- Pulse log every cycle: `dispatch_triage_reviews: thinking and standard model resolution failed`; `Dispatch_capacity: ... provider=unknown provider_accounts_total=0`.

## Root cause

`resolve_api_key` Source 4 (`model-availability-helper.sh` ~L387-420) only reads `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`. OpenCode 2 no longer writes that file, and the OAuth pool (`oauth-pool.json`) is only used as a cooldown/auth-error *blocker* (`_probe_oauth_pool_cooldown_gate`), never as a positive credential source.

## Suggested fix

Treat a provider as `oauth-refresh-available` (healthy, skip HTTP probe) when either:
1. `opencode auth list` (or the OpenCode 2 credential store) reports an OAuth credential for the provider, or
2. `oauth-pool.json` has at least one non-errored, non-cooling account for the provider.

Do not recommend writing a token-less `auth.json` as a workaround: OpenCode 2 may import a legacy `auth.json` and overwrite the stored credential.

## Verification

- `model-availability-helper.sh probe anthropic --force` → healthy via OAuth.
- `model-availability-helper.sh resolve standard` → `anthropic/claude-sonnet-*`.
- Next pulse cycle shows a non-empty provider in `Dispatch_capacity` and dispatches an `auto-dispatch` issue.

## Task


Add a reusable `cloudron-helper.sh nginx-http2 <off|on|status> <server>` subcommand that turns HTTP/2 off on a Cloudron host's managed nginx during an HTTP/2 CVE window, keeps it off when Cloudron regenerates configs, reports state, and restores HTTP/2 exactly afterwards. Optionally `--sctp-block` / `--sctp-unblock` for the SCTP escalation step.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/cloudron-helper.sh`. Add a `nginx-http2` case next to `"health" | "fleet-health")`, reusing `health_check`'s server lookup (`jq .servers.<name>.ip/ssh_port` from `$CONFIG_FILE`) and its `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` pattern.
- The remote side is a small embedded script installed to `/usr/local/sbin/aidevops-nginx-http2` and run by `/etc/cron.d/aidevops-nginx-http2` (every 2 min). The `apply` mode:
  - edits only when `http2\s+on\s*;` or `listen[^;]*\shttp2` is present;
  - backs up the real directory (0600, keeping 10);
  - appends legacy-listen files to `/var/lib/aidevops-nginx-http2/legacy-listen-files.txt`;
  - runs `nginx -t`, restoring the backup if it fails, otherwise reloads;
  - logs via `logger -t aidevops-nginx-http2`.
- `status` prints KEY=VALUE: `h2_on_files`, `h2_off_files`, `legacy_listen_recorded`, `cron`, `sctp_blocked`, `sctp_loaded`, and `running_new_binary` (`/proc/<nginx master>/exe` not `(deleted)`).
- The `on` (revert) mode:
  - removes the cron;
  - turns `http2 off;` back into `http2 on;`;
  - restores ` http2` after `ssl` on `listen ... 443 ssl` lines of recorded files only;
  - runs `nginx -t` (rollback on failure), then `systemctl restart nginx`.
- `--patched-marker CVE-ID` (optional): `apply` becomes a no-op once `zgrep -q <CVE> /usr/share/doc/nginx-common/changelog.Debian.gz` matches, and `on` refuses until it matches unless `--force`.
- Reference implementation (private, working, ShellCheck-clean): the session's host script had `apply|status|revert` modes with exactly the above logic. Re-derive from this brief; do not copy host-specific paths.
- EDIT: `.agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md`. In "nginx security releases" (added by t19117), point the mitigation bullets at the new subcommand, and add it to the Quick Reference `Commands` list.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-helper.sh`
- `.agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add a reusable `cloudron-helper.sh nginx-http2 <off|on|status> <server>` subcommand that turns HTTP/2 off on a Cloudron host's managed nginx during an HTTP/2 CVE window, keeps it off when Cloudron regenerates configs, reports state, and restores HTTP/2 exactly afterwards. Optionally `--sctp-block` / `--sctp-unblock` for the SCTP escalation step.

## Why

During the nginx2root response (advisory `nginx2root-2026-11`, t19117 / GH#39093) the interim mitigation had to be invented by hand per host. Observed traps that a one-line `sed` gets wrong, all on Cloudron 10.1.6 / Ubuntu 26.04:

- Vhosts in `/etc/nginx/applications/<app-id>/*.conf` use both `http2 on;` and the legacy `listen 443 ssl http2;`. The legacy form enables HTTP/2 for the whole address:port.
- Cloudron rewrote 1–2 vhosts per host about 2 minutes after a reboot, so a one-off edit reverts silently. A guarded re-apply from `/etc/cron.d` every 2 minutes was needed.
- `/etc/nginx` is a symlink into Cloudron's `platformdata/nginx`. `tar -C / etc/nginx` archives only the link, so the backup must target `readlink -f /etc/nginx`.
- An exact revert needs a record of which files used the legacy listen form. `box` regeneration after reboot does not rewrite every vhost.
- The `turn` container (coturn) holds kernel SCTP sockets, so SCTP blocking needs a modprobe.d entry plus a reboot.

Next nginx/HTTP/2 CVE, users should run one command instead of rebuilding this.

## Acceptance

- `cloudron-helper.sh nginx-http2 status <server>` prints the KEY=VALUE state, read-only.
- `off` leaves zero files matching either HTTP/2 form, installs the cron, and `nginx -t` passes. External `curl -sI --http2 --resolve <fqdn>:443:<ip> https://<fqdn>/` shows `HTTP/1.1`.
- `on` restores both forms byte-identically for recorded files (diff against the pre-`off` backup shows no `listen`/`http2` differences) and removes the cron.
- ShellCheck zero violations; every function has explicit `return`; `local var="$1"` style.

title: t19119: pulse: Bash 3.2-safe tracked-PID capacity waits in the parallel dispatch loop
body:
## Task


Replace the two `wait -n` capacity waits in the parallel dispatch loop with a Bash 3.2-compatible wait on tracked PIDs, so evaluation concurrency stays bounded by `max_parallel` when the pulse runs under Bash 3.2.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Replace the two `wait -n` capacity waits in the parallel dispatch loop with a Bash 3.2-compatible wait on tracked PIDs, so evaluation concurrency stays bounded by `max_parallel` when the pulse runs under Bash 3.2.

## Why

`wait -n` requires Bash 4.3+. `shared-constants.sh` re-execs under a modern bash only when one is installed. Without one, the pulse keeps running under Bash 3.2. There, `wait -n` always fails, and `_dispatch_max_wait_for_capacity` treats that failure as GH#21729 PID reuse. It purges every PID from `_pids` and starts the next evaluation. Concurrency is then unbounded, and the end-of-loop cleanup can no longer wait for the discarded children.

t19116 (PR #39092) bounds worker launches independently through the launch-slot semaphore (mkdir test-and-set), so this gap affects evaluation fan-out and API load, not launch count. With the gate's default 3x evaluation oversubscription, the fan-out is larger when the cap fails. Raised by CodeRabbit on PR #39092. The finding is about base-revision code, so it is filed separately here.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`, `_dispatch_max_wait_for_capacity` (rg `GH#21729: if wait -n fails`): replace `wait -n` with a poll over the tracked `_pids`. Reap exited PIDs with `kill -0` plus `wait "$pid"`, keep live PIDs, and sleep briefly between polls. Never clear live PIDs on a failed wait.
- Same file, the reservation-reconciliation wait (rg `wait -n found no children while reconciling reservations`): same change.
- Reuse or follow the pattern of `_dispatch_max_wait_tracked_pids` in the same file (rg `^_dispatch_max_wait_tracked_pids\(\)`), which already waits on tracked PIDs at loop end.
- Update the header comment (rg `Concurrency cap is enforced via`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`

## Acceptance

- No `wait -n` remains in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`.
- Under `/bin/bash` 3.2 (macOS), the parallel loop never runs more than `max_parallel` evaluations at once.
- The existing GH#21729 stale-PID protection still holds: a reused PID that is not a child never blocks the loop.

On macOS with the stock `/usr/bin/python3` (3.9.6, no `tomli`), `./setup.sh --non-interactive` exits 1 at the `update_codex_config` stage:

title: Cloudron commits-mode standing policy still rejects upstreamLicense.url full-SHA bumps (GH#38359 half-fixed)
body:
## What

A commit-mode (`upstream_mode: "commits"`) standing release policy still cannot authorize a real routine bump of a commit-tracked Cloudron package. Every such bump also moves `upstreamLicense.url` (`https://github.com/<upstream>/blob/<full sha>/LICENSE`), and the predicate rejects any manifest change beyond `version`/`upstreamVersion` in commits mode.

title: Pulse: skip a cycle of worker dispatch when the systemd worker backend probe fails at cycle start
body:
## What

When the selected systemd worker backend is unavailable at pulse cycle start, the pulse should skip worker dispatch for that cycle (and say why once) instead of claiming issues and failing every launch.

Follow-up split out of #39028, which fixes the cause: the sudo approval kick started an unmanaged pulse without the user session bus. This issue is the defence in depth for any other way a pulse can start without `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` / `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`.

## Why

Evidence in #39028: one cycle with no user bus made five launches fail across three issues in about 10 minutes. Each one claimed the issue, failed with `manager_probe_failed`, and rolled the claim back. That is wasted claim/comment churn, and that pulse also held the lock that the timer pulse needed.

## Reproducer

From #39028 (Ubuntu, systemd user-service pulse, v3.39.228): a pulse started with `sudo -u <user> -H -- pulse-wrapper.sh`, with no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, held the pulse lock and logged on every dispatch:

    [dispatch_worker_launch] ERROR: selected systemd backend unavailable for #<n> (reason=manager_probe_failed rc=1 ...); detached fallback suppressed
    [dispatch_worker_launch] ERROR: worker spawn failed for #<n> rc=1; no worker submitted (GH#36390)

To reproduce locally on Linux: `env -u XDG_RUNTIME_DIR -u DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` with an eligible `auto-dispatch` issue queued.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`

The cycle-level caller may live in a different `pulse-dispatch-*.sh` file. Confirm it with the `rg` command below and record the actual path.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh:240-273` `_dlw_systemd_user_service_available` already classifies the backend (`manager_probe_failed`, `missing_systemctl`, ...). Reuse it as is.
- Call it once per cycle before the dispatch phase claims anything, only when the selected backend is systemd. Find the dispatch-phase entry with `rg -n "dispatch_worker_launch|_dlw_launch_systemd_worker" .agents/scripts/pulse-*.sh`; the exact caller path must be found that way.
- On failure, log one line, for example `[pulse] dispatch skipped this cycle: systemd worker backend unavailable (reason=...)`, skip claim/launch for the cycle, and still run the non-dispatch phases (merge, housekeeping). Do not fall back to detached launches: that is suppressed on purpose.
- Do not change launchd/macOS behaviour.

## Acceptance

- With `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` unset on Linux under the systemd backend, one pulse cycle logs the skip line once, makes no dispatch claims, and produces no `worker spawn failed` lines.

title: t19121: fix(planning): protected-branch planning PR fallback overwrites newer default-branch TODO rows from a stale caller snapshot
body:
## Task


Make the protected-branch planning PR fallback in `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh` merge the caller's planning edits onto `origin/<default>`, rather than overwriting whole files with the caller's copy. Then apply the same stale-snapshot task-regression guard that the direct publisher uses.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the protected-branch planning PR fallback in `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh` merge the caller's planning edits onto `origin/<default>`, rather than overwriting whole files with the caller's copy. Then apply the same stale-snapshot task-regression guard that the direct publisher uses.

## Why

PR #39114 was opened by `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: add t19120 ..."` from a feature worktree whose `HEAD` predated two newer TODO rows on `main` (t19119/GH#39103 and t19118/GH#39098). The PR diff added t19120 and silently deleted both rows. A review bot caught it, and an interactive session had to restore the rows by hand. If the deletion had merged, two dispatchable tasks would have disappeared from TODO.md without warning.

Root cause: `_todo_copy_planning_changes_to_worktree` (rg `^_todo_copy_planning_changes_to_worktree\(\)`) runs `cp -p` on each changed file from the caller checkout into a fresh `origin/<default>` worktree. Any change that landed on the default branch after the caller's `HEAD` is reverted. The direct path in `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh` already avoids this. `_planning_publish_build_index` three-way merges each file with base = caller `HEAD` blob, ours = caller working copy and theirs = remote parent blob (rg `merge-file -p --diff3`). Then `_planning_publish_guard_task_regression` (GH#35062) refuses deletion or un-completion of task lines that the commit message does not name. Every repo whose default branch requires PRs for planning files (including this one) takes the fallback path, so the guard never runs where it matters most.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh`, `_todo_copy_planning_changes_to_worktree`: for each changed path, resolve base = `git -C "$repo_path" rev-parse HEAD:<path>` (or absent), ours = caller working file (or absent) and theirs = the worktree's `origin/<default>` file (or absent).
  - If theirs equals base, keep the current copy behaviour.
  - If ours equals base, leave theirs.
  - If ours equals theirs, there is nothing to do.
  - Otherwise run `git merge-file -p --diff3 ours base theirs`. On rc 1, a conflict, or any add/delete-versus-modify mix, fail with a retryable, explicit message: refresh from the default branch and re-apply. Do not write a partial file.
  - Mirror the decision table in `_planning_publish_build_index` (`.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`, rg `if \[\[ "\$parent_blob" != "\$origin_sha" \]\]`).
- After the copy and merge and before the commit in `_todo_commit_planning_worktree`, run the task-regression check against the worktree's TODO.md files. Compare `origin/<default>` with the staged result and pass `commit_msg`. Reuse `_planning_publish_task_states` and `_planning_publish_guard_task_regression` if `planning-publisher.sh` is already sourced at that point (check `planning-commit-helper.sh` source order). Otherwise extract the awk comparison into a shared function instead of duplicating it.
- Keep the existing publication identity, branch reuse, label provisioning, source cleanup and recovery receipts unchanged.
- Touch `planning-publisher.sh` only if the guard must be extracted for sharing. The test file below is new (see Verification).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-todo-commit-planning-pr-merge.sh`

## Acceptance

- Caller `HEAD` lacks rows that `origin/main` gained later, and the caller adds one new row. The planning PR branch then contains all the `origin/main` rows plus the new row: zero deletions in `git diff origin/main..<branch> -- TODO.md`.
- If the caller's change conflicts with `origin/main` on the same lines, publication fails before pushing, with the retry message. Caller planning edits are preserved, not cleaned.
- If the caller deletes or un-completes a task that its commit message does not name, publication is refused before pushing. Naming the task in the message allows it, as in the direct path.
- Existing publication behaviour (branch reuse, noop, label provisioning, recovery output) is unchanged.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh` (and `planning-publisher.sh` if touched): zero findings.
- New focused test using a temporary bare origin plus a clone with a protected-default stub (see `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-todo-commit-home-fallback.sh` for the sourcing and stub pattern): stale-base add, conflicting edit and unnamed deletion cases.
- Existing: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-todo-commit-home-fallback.sh` and the planning-publisher tests (`rg -l planning-publisher .agents/scripts/tests`).

## Context

- Evidence: PR #39114 first commit `7f1d7bd7` (+1/-3 on TODO.md). Fixed by follow-up commit `f136d5ba` (+2/-0 against `main`). Review thread `discussion_r4623287329`.

title: fix(validators): reduce plugin test concurrency under moderate host load (follow-up to GH#35499)
body:
## What

The full-loop plugin validator still fails on timing-sensitive process tests when the host is busy but below the serialization threshold from GH#35499. Lower or graduate the threshold so moderately loaded hosts get reduced concurrency instead of default `node --test` parallelism.

## Why

`_validator_plugin_test_concurrency` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh:332` serializes only when the 1-minute load average exceeds 4 per CPU (64 on a 16-CPU Mac). It samples once, before the suite starts, and the suite itself then adds about 15 parallel test files that each spawn process trees.

On 2026-11-19, while running `commit-and-pr` for PR #39132 (a pricing/docs change), the "running plugin tests serially" line never appeared, and each run failed in a different unrelated test:

- `tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:53` — `wait-aware status ...` got `'failed'` where `'succeeded'` was expected (4.4 s, against 1.9 s when run alone)
- `tests/test-worker-blocker-log.mjs:406,420` — `blocker logger exited 1` (parallel appenders)
- `tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs:129` — `termination_cause` was `'post_exit_cleanup'` where `null` was expected, at a load average of about 58 (3.6 per CPU, just under the threshold)
- two runs hit `TIMEOUT after 300s` and `TIMEOUT after 900s`

Each failing file passes alone. The full suite passed directly once the load dropped. The validator then passed on the first try with `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY=4`.

## Reproducer

On a 16-CPU host with other workers running (1-minute load about 40-64, i.e. below 4 per CPU), run `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue <N> ...` on a branch that touches `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`.

- Observed: the plugin tests run at default concurrency, and one or more of the timing tests above fail, or the suite hits the validator timeout.
- Expected: reduced concurrency is selected and the suite passes.
- Confirmation: `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY=4` on the same host makes it pass.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh` `_validator_plugin_test_concurrency`: graduate by load per CPU. For example, above 4 → 1 (unchanged), above 1.5 → `max(2, floor(cpus/4))`, otherwise unset. Print the chosen value. Respect an existing caller-set `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY`.
- Keep the GH#35499 rule: never extend timeouts or budgets.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh` clean.
- With a stubbed load (or `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY` preset), the helper prints the selected concurrency, and `npm run test` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops` receives `--test-concurrency=<n>`.
- Run `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` on a plugin-touching branch while other workers are active (load 2-4 per CPU); the plugin validator passes without manual env overrides.

title: t19125: Reset-aware OAuth pool rotation: prefer the account whose quota resets soonest
body:
## Task


Rotation over Anthropic OAuth seats with equal priority prefers the seat whose usage window (weekly first) resets soonest, provided that seat still has usable quota. In effect it is earliest-deadline-first, so quota that would expire unused gets spent before quota with more runway. title: routine-log-helper: create-issue persists multi-line issue_number (stderr mixed into URL capture)
body:
## Bug

`routine-log-helper.sh create-issue` stores a multi-line `issue_number` in `cron/<id>/routine-state.json`, e.g. `"issue_number": "37993\n18"` instead of `"18"`. Observed on every core routine (r901-r914) on v3.39.232 after `init-routines`.

## Cause (verified in source)

`.agents/scripts/routine-log-helper.sh:1031-1033` captures the issue URL with `issue_url=$(gh_create_issue ... 2>&1)`, so stderr lines from the wrapper are mixed into the value. Line 1041 then runs `grep -oE '[0-9]+$'`, which matches a trailing number on every line, producing a two-line result. The value is persisted without validation (around line 1054) and returned as the existing issue on later calls. `init-routines-helper.sh` survives only because it takes `tail -1` of the output; the run-update paths (`gh_issue_edit_safe "$issue_number"` and similar) receive the raw multi-line value, so routine tracking issues likely never receive run results.

## Fix

1. Drop `2>&1` from the capture (log stderr separately) and extract only the last `/issues/<n>` match.
2. Refuse to persist any `issue_number` not matching `^[0-9]+$`.
3. Normalise to the last numeric line on read, so existing broken state heals without manual edits.

## Verification

```bash
for f in ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/cron/r9*/routine-state.json; do
  jq -e '.issue_number|tostring|test("^[0-9]+$")' "$f" >/dev/null || echo "BAD $f"
done   # expect no output
```

Acceptance: every state file holds a numeric issue number; tracking issues update after a run; a second `create-issue` does not create a duplicate issue (negative).

title: research-only subagent cannot read registered repos outside the session directory
body:
## Problem

The `research-only` subagent cannot read repositories registered in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` when they live outside the parent session's directory. Build+ guidance routes all research-only discovery to `research-only` ("never `general` or `explore`"), so multi-repo audits from a hub session fail: every Read/Grep/Glob on a sibling repo returns `Permission denied: external_directory`.

Observed on v3.39.232 / OpenCode 2.3.0: a hub session delegated read-only audits of two registered sibling repos outside the hub directory; both research-only children were fully blocked, while an `explore` child read the same files without issue (the global config allows them).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/build-plus.md`
- `.agents/reference/research-staging.md`

> Maintainer edit: the reporter scoped `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs`. The maintainer review moved the scope to the guidance files. See "Maintainer resolution" below.

## Cause

`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-agent-profiles.mjs` `addResearchStagingPermissions()` (around line 289) sets the research-only profile's `external_directory` to `{ "*": "deny" }` plus only the research-staging directory. Registered repos are never added.

## Proposal

Allow read-only `external_directory` access for the `path` of every repo in `repos.json` (and their linked worktrees under `worktree_base_dir`), keeping the existing credential-name denies (`.env`, `.env.*`, `.npmrc`, `credential*`, etc.) applied under each allowed root. Optionally gate with a config key (e.g. `research_only.registered_repos: true`, default on).

## Acceptance

- A research-only child can Read/Grep/Glob any registered repo path from a session rooted elsewhere.
- `.env`, `.npmrc`, `credential*` and the other denied names remain blocked inside those roots (negative).
- Unregistered paths under `~/` remain denied (negative).

## Maintainer resolution (supersedes Proposal and Acceptance above)

The defect is real, but it sits in the routing guidance, not in the permission profile. The `research-only` deny-all `external_directory` envelope is a deliberate boundary: GH#28703 / #28768, `reference/research-staging.md`: "All sibling external directories remain denied". Do **not** change `config-agent-profiles.mjs` or `tools/ai-assistants/research-only.md`. The contradiction is in `.agents/build-plus.md:92`, which sends *all* read-only discovery to `research-only` and offers no route for targets outside the session root.

### Implementation

1. `.agents/build-plus.md:92`: limit the rule to what the profile can reach, and point to the cross-repo route. Replacement for the first sentence:

   ```markdown
   Research-only discovery inside the session root or staged artifacts uses
   `research-only`, never `general` or `explore`; for other repositories follow
   `reference/research-staging.md` "Cross-repository research".
   ```

2. `.agents/build-plus.md:98` (Deliberation bullet): change "launch at most 2 focused Explore agents" to "launch at most 2 focused `research-only` agents". The bullet currently contradicts line 92.
3. `.agents/reference/research-staging.md`: add a `## Cross-repository research` section before `## Independent code review`, with this content (wording may be tightened, semantics may not change):

   ```markdown
   ## Cross-repository research

   `research-only` cannot read registered repositories or linked worktrees
   outside the session root; this is intentional and must not be widened per
   repository. For read-only discovery in another repository:

   1. Search it directly from the primary session (`rg`/`git -C <repo> grep`,
      then targeted Read).
   2. To delegate bounded analysis, stage regular files or a
      `review-evidence-helper.sh bundle` output into a task child here and pass
      that path, or pass excerpts to `ai-research` via `files`.
   3. For a whole-repository audit, run it from a session rooted in that
      repository.

   Do not substitute `general` or `explore`; they are not fail-closed.
   ```

### Acceptance

- `rg -n "research-only|Explore" .agents/build-plus.md` shows no instruction that routes out-of-root discovery to `research-only` and no remaining "Explore agents" routing.
- `reference/research-staging.md` documents the three cross-repo routes. The existing "All sibling external directories remain denied" boundary statement is unchanged.
- Negative: `git diff --stat origin/main` touches only the two files in Files Scope. `config-agent-profiles.mjs` and `research-only.md` are unchanged.

### Verification

- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` (markdown checks) passes for the two files.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-research-only-profile.mjs` still passes. This proves the permission envelope is untouched.

title: fix(routines): preserve user enabled/disabled state for core routines across routines TODO.md regeneration
body:
## What

Keep a user's enabled/disabled choice (`- [x]` / `- [ ]`) for **core** routines when `init-routines-helper.sh` regenerates the routines repo `TODO.md`.

## Why

`_write_todo_md()` (`.agents/scripts/init-routines-helper.sh:55-100`) keeps the `## User Routines` tail, but rewrites every `## Core Routines (framework-managed)` line from `get_core_routine_entries`, using the framework default `enabled` field. Every setup or `aidevops update` runs `scaffold_repo` → `_write_todo_md` (directly for new repos, or through `_publish_routines_scaffold` for existing remotes, `init-routines-helper.sh:565-650`). That publishes the default `[x]` back over the user's `[ ]`.

This contradicts the generated header comment ("Edit only the enabled/disabled state here") and the documented pause path (`init-routines-helper.sh:852-853`: "Change `- [x] ${rid}` to `- [ ] ${rid}` in the routines repo TODO.md"). Found while reviewing #39145. There, a user could not turn off a routine that failed on every run, because their pause was reverted on the next setup.

## Reproducer

Reproduced against `main` @ `83390d35d1`. A scratch dir contains a `TODO.md` with `- [ ] r924 Cloudron releases ...` in the core section and `- [x] r001 Example ...` under `## User Routines`. Run:

```bash
source .agents/scripts/init-routines-helper.sh
DRY_RUN=false
_write_todo_md "$scratch"
grep -E '^- \[( |x)\] r924 |^- \[( |x)\] r001 ' "$scratch/TODO.md"
```

Output:

```text
- [x] r924 Cloudron releases — process signed approvals repeat:cron(*/30 * * * *) ~3m run:scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply
- [x] r001 Example repeat:daily(@09:00) ~5m run:custom/scripts/example.sh
```

The paused `r924` came back as `[x]`. The user routine was preserved.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/init-routines-helper.sh`

## How

- `.agents/scripts/init-routines-helper.sh` `_write_todo_md()`: before overwriting, read the existing file's core-section lines (`^- \[( |x)\] (r[0-9]+) `). Store `rid → state`. When emitting each core entry, use the recorded state when present. Otherwise use the framework default (new routines keep their default). Do not carry over any other field. Schedule, title and script stay framework-owned.
- Bash 3.2 compatible: no associative arrays. Use a newline-delimited `rid state` list and `awk`/`grep -E "^${rid} "`, the same pattern the file already uses to extract `existing_tail`.
- Reference pattern: the existing `existing_tail` preservation in the same function.

## Acceptance

- Pausing a core routine (`- [ ] r924 ...`) and re-running `_write_todo_md` keeps `[ ]`. Its schedule, title and script still refresh from `core-routines.sh`.
- A core routine that is new to the existing file gets its framework default state.
- Removed core routines are not resurrected from the old file.
- `## User Routines` content is preserved unchanged (existing behaviour).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-routines.sh` (this test already calls `_write_todo_md` against a temp root) and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-init-routines-readonly-guard.sh` pass.

title: fix(runtime): detect output-limit (finish: length) responses and steer to sectioned writes
body:
## What

Detect when an assistant response hits OpenCode's request output limit (`finish: length`, with the in-flight tool call aborted) and tell the model why it stopped, so it switches to sectioned writes instead of losing the work or repeating it.

## Why

OpenCode caps each response at 32,000 output tokens (`HOST_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX`, `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-limits.mjs:87`). When a model tries to write a large file in one Write call, the response ends with finish reason `length`. The tool call is aborted as `Tool execution aborted` and nothing is saved. Headless `opencode run` then exits silently.

Evidence:

- Fable 5.2 scene build, 2026-11-17: two `length` responses saved nothing and cost $3.05 of the run's $8.59 API-equivalent cost. The fix was a raised limit plus sectioned writes (now documented in `.agents/tools/design/blender-scripted-scenes.md`, but only Blender work reads that guide).
- This project's interactive session DB alone shows 17 `length` finishes across 12 sessions and 5 models (claude-haiku-5-5 ×9, gpt-5.6-sol ×4, claude-fable-5-2 ×2, gpt-5.5 ×1, claude-opus-5-5 ×1).
- No framework code detects this. `rg -i "finish.{0,20}length"` across the plugin and `.agents/scripts` finds nothing. In `headless-runtime-helper.sh:519`, `premature_exit` resumes with a generic completion contract that does not mention the output limit, so the resumed model can hit the same limit again.

## Reproducer

Trigger: in any OpenCode session, ask the model to write one file of more than about 2,500 lines in a single Write call.

**Symptom command:** `sqlite3 -readonly -header -column <data>/opencode.db "select data->>'modelID' model, count(*) length_finishes, count(distinct session_id) sessions, round(sum(data->>'cost'),2) cost from message where data->>'role'='assistant' and data->>'finish'='length' group by 1 order by 2 desc"`

**Actual output** (project interactive DB, 2026-11-19):

```text
model             length_finishes  sessions  cost
claude-haiku-5-5  9                5         1.13
gpt-5.6-sol       4                4         0.0
claude-fable-5-2  2                1         3.05
gpt-5.5           1                1         0.0
claude-opus-5-5   1                1         0.82
```

**Expected:** after a `length` finish, the next turn or headless resume is told the cause and writes in sections. Currently nothing tells it, and the Write tool part shows `Tool execution aborted` with no file saved.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-turn-state.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh` (scope recovery: the premature-exit resume prompt is built here, in `_handle_cmd_run_continuation_attempt`; the helper cannot change it without this one-line hook)
- ADD: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-output-limit-notice.mjs`

1. **Plugin, interactive and headless.** On `message.updated` for an assistant message with `finish === "length"`, record a one-shot flag for the session. Follow the existing per-session state pattern in `session-turn-state.mjs`. On the next system transform for that session, inject one short note: "Your previous response hit the 32K output-token limit and its tool call was discarded; nothing was written. Write large files in sections of under ~120 lines (Write, then Edit appends)." Clear the flag after injecting.
2. **Headless resume.** Where `premature_exit` → `resume_session_with_completion_contract` is chosen (`headless-runtime-helper.sh:519`), detect a final `length` finish from the session (DB query or exported messages). Classify it as `output_clamp` and add the sectioned-write instruction to the resume prompt.
3. Do **not** raise `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_MAX` by default. OpenCode compacts at context minus this limit (`model-limits.mjs:93-104`), so raising it costs compaction headroom and only moves the cliff. Keep it as the documented opt-in for deliberate long-output delegations.

## Verification

- Plugin: a unit test in the existing session-turn-state test style. A synthetic `message.updated` with `finish: "length"` produces exactly one injected note on the next transform and none after that.
- Headless: the `output_clamp` classification is chosen for a session whose last assistant message has `finish: length`, and the resume prompt contains the sectioned-write instruction.
- `node --test` for the touched plugin tests; ShellCheck clean on `headless-runtime-helper.sh`.

title: project-node-runtime: worker prelaunch ignores /usr/local/bin and unversioned Homebrew node that satisfy engines
body:
## What

`_project_node_bin` in `.agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh` aborts worker prelaunch with `project_node_environment_failure` even when an installed Node satisfies the project's `engines.node`, because it never considers the official macOS installer location `/usr/local/bin/node` (unless that happens to be first on PATH).

## Observed

- macOS arm64. PATH resolves `node` to a v22.22.3 copy in `~/.local/bin` (installed by another tool). `/usr/local/bin/node` is v24.13.0 from the nodejs.org pkg installer.
- Project pins `.node-version` 22.23.5 and `engines.node: ">=22.23.4"`.
- `headless-prelaunch.log`: `prelaunch_abort ... cause=project_node_environment_failure` for two workers in a row; the issues stayed queued.
- Candidates scanned (lines ~92-107): current `node`, fnm, nvm, volta, mise, `<brew>/opt/node@*/bin/node`, n. Plain `/usr/local/bin/node` and `/opt/homebrew/bin/node` (unversioned `node` formula) are not candidates, so pass 2 ("any hard-compatible runtime") cannot find v24 even though it satisfies `>=22.23.4`.
- Workaround applied: `brew install node@22` (then `brew unlink` to keep the user's default PATH), after which the resolver returns `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin`.

## Proposed fix

Add the standard system install locations to the candidate list after the version-manager caches: `/usr/local/bin/node`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/node`, `${HOMEBREW_PREFIX}/bin/node`, and `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node` (deduplicated, `-x` checked). Pass 1 still prefers exact pins; pass 2 can then pick any installed runtime that satisfies `engines`.

## Verification

Extend the existing project-node-runtime test with a fake `/usr/local`-style prefix (overridable like `AIDEVOPS_NODE_BREW_PREFIXES`) containing a satisfying node while PATH holds an older one; the resolver should print that bin dir and return 0.

- .agents/scripts/project-node-runtime.sh

title: t19129: fix(checkpoint-continuation): treat temp_dir_recovery releases as stall-class so draft checkpoints continue instead of parking for attention

## What

A `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=temp_dir_recovery` release on an issue with a worker draft checkpoint PR is treated as a stall-class release, so the draft gets an immediate exact-head continuation instead of a `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` record that parks it for the 12h attention re-arm window.

## Why

`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:1400-1409` (GH#35128) releases the claim as `temp_dir_recovery` when the OpenCode permission broker stops a worker for writing outside the project (e.g. host `/tmp`). Its comment states the intent: "owned recovery (use AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR); no maintainer hold. Release the claim so the issue is redispatched." Without a draft PR that is what happens. With a draft checkpoint, `temp_dir_recovery` is missing from every stall-release list, so `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` falls through to `_pcc_completed_attention` and posts `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION ... reason=temp_dir_recovery`. Ordinary redispatch then stays blocked (`worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`) until the 43200s re-arm, so a runtime-only interruption costs 12h+ per occurrence.

Evidence (2026-11-19): three open issues in a private managed repo (one with a draft checkpoint PR parked since 2026-11-18) carry `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION ... reason=temp_dir_recovery`; 46 issues across managed repos have had `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=temp_dir_recovery`. The runtime, not the worker, ended these attempts, so no worker decision about completeness exists — the same condition as the existing stall classes (`watchdog_kill:*`, `worker_incomplete_exit`).

## How

### Reference pattern

Model on how `worker_claim_ready_transition_failed` / `worker_incomplete_exit` are listed as stall-class releases in all four mirrors below; keep the four lists consistent (their comments already say they mirror each other).

title: Worker PRs open against main when the repo default branch is dev; guard the PR base
body:
## What

Worker PRs in managed repos whose default branch is `dev` are sometimes opened against `main`. Guard `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` (and the merge pass) so a worker PR targets the remote default branch unless `--base` names a genuine stacked parent.

## Observed evidence (one runner, 2026-11-18..19)

- Three worker PRs in two private managed repos (default branch `dev`, a release-only `main` with a ruleset `update` restriction) were created with base `main`.
- Effects: (1) the PR diff carried the dev/main divergence (one showed 58 files including two `.github/workflows/*` files it never touched, so the merge pass skipped it with "modifies workflow files but token lacks workflow scope"); (2) `Resolves #N` did not link, because closing keywords only apply on the default branch; (3) `full-loop-helper.sh merge` failed with "the base branch policy prohibits the merge" while all required checks were green; (4) unrelated CI failures from the divergence were routed to CI fix-workers.
- Retargeting with `gh pr edit N --base dev` fixed each one: the diff shrank to the PR's own commits and one PR merged immediately.
- Root cause of the `main` base is NOT established. `_resolve_pr_base_branch` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` (lines ~252-262) uses the remote default branch unless `FULL_LOOP_STACK_BASE` is set by `--base` (added for stacked PRs, GH#37578). Candidates: a worker passing `--base main`, a raw `gh pr create --base main`, or a `branch.<name>.gh-merge-base` config. No `Stacked PR: base is origin/main` line was found in the runner logs, so the path is unknown.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` `_validate_stack_base`: refuse `--base` when it names a long-lived branch that is not a stacked parent (for example any branch other than the default that matches the repo's protected/ruleset branches, or `main`/`master` when the default branch differs), with an error naming the default branch.
2. Merge pass (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` gate chain): when a worker-origin PR's `baseRefName` differs from the repo default branch and the head branch is not a stacked child of another open PR, retarget to the default branch with an audit comment (or route it once with that diagnosis) instead of routing CI fix-workers.
3. Add one log line in `commit-and-pr` stating the chosen base and its source (default / `--base` / gh config) so the root cause is visible next time.

## Verification

- Existing stacked-PR tests (`.agents/scripts/tests/` around `commit-and-pr --base`) still pass.
- A fixture repo with default `dev` and a `main` branch: `commit-and-pr --base main` without a stacked parent fails with the new error; with no `--base` the PR targets `dev`.

title: browser-qa-helper screenshot exits 1 on Linux without sips/magick even when images are within max-dim
body:
## Observed

On Linux without ImageMagick, `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot` captures every screenshot and prints valid JSON results, then exits 1 with:

```text
[ERROR] No supported image tool found for guardrails (need sips or magick)
[ERROR] Screenshot guardrail enforcement failed
```

This happened even though every capture was already within `--max-dim 1568` (375x667 and 1440x900 viewports, no `--full-page`). Callers that trust the exit code treat a successful visual check as a failure.

Reproduce (any public URL, Linux host with neither `sips` nor `magick` on PATH):

```bash
browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url https://example.com --pages / --viewports mobile,desktop --max-dim 1568 --output-dir "$AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR/qa"
echo $?   # 1, though the PNGs and JSON are fine
```

## Expected

When no resize tool is available, read the PNG dimensions (the IHDR header is enough: bytes 16-23) and pass if every image is within `--max-dim`. Fail only when an image actually exceeds the limit and cannot be resized. Optionally fall back to Python Pillow or Playwright's own `clip`/viewport sizing before failing.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh`: the screenshot guardrail step that looks for `sips` or `magick`.
- `.agents/reference/screenshot-limits.md`: document the Linux fallback.

## Verification

Run the reproduce command on a Linux host without ImageMagick: it should exit 0 with the same JSON. Then pass a `--full-page` capture taller than 1568px: it should still fail with a clear message naming the oversized file.
